# Separation <note>original: "Separatio"; in astrology, this refers to a planet moving away from an aspect with another, often signifying the fading of an influence</note>

These are called circumstances, and they involve worthlessness and permanence, for life and [virtue] <note>reading "vitatem" as "virtutem" or "vitalitatem"</note> are where evil comes from. And if they are applied correctly to signs of evil, the end result makes it good. These present things in the metallic and non-volatile <note>perhaps referring to alchemical qualities assigned to the Lots</note> that proceed before individual scruples <term>scruples: very small astronomical measurements, 1/60th of a degree</term>. Let him know that concerning these things, he who makes [the judgment] 
<margin>Judgment of the Parts <note>original: "Iudiciū patrī" (iudicium partium)</note></margin>
knows that the reason is not broken, as the principal part [is judged]. It is well when [the planet] is at the world, and there are two spirits [influencing] with others, which fall from the houses of evil. Where it begins and others fall in each of the houses, and it is of two hands [influences] for one. And even if the part does not fall in other houses, the spirits of the body, just as three [portions] of holy water, might fall into the hand of the house. The part which is held in every spirit is strengthened when it is applied to the cause [the planetary aspect]. Besides the sign, it says two [points] for the application. Two and two from every part, and the stronger among them, and that which holds the spirits, is outward when they appear because then all the spirits [act] through the strength and equality [of the aspect]. And if some appear and others do not, the part would be imperfect. # Concerning the Change of the Present Weather
Intending to go beyond the doctrines <note>original: "rolina," likely a corruption of "doctrina" or a specific philosophical reference</note> of the philosophers, as every change of the air <note>The author uses "aeris" to mean both the atmosphere and the weather.</note> occurs from the conjunction of the figures or the stars that exist within them, and from the movements of the planets themselves, and their relationships to the bodies. To understand this, we must first gather the signs and stars within them, and the applications of the planets according to certain rules, so that the change of the weather may be understood.

**Aries** thunders and flashes with lightning; it causes heavy rains and moderate winds. It brings either great heat or mortality; it heats and then ceases, cooling the southern regions.

**Taurus** generally brings heavy waters and falls, yet it inclines more toward heat. It affects the earth with the Pleiades <note>A star cluster in Taurus historically associated with rain and storms.</note>, which cause earthquakes and winds; it makes clouds and smoke, moistens, and cools. It thunders and creates disturbances in the earth and fires.

**Aries** <note>The text repeats Aries here, likely referring to its northern/southern divisions.</note> in the north and south is unstable and causes disordered movements.

**Gemini** makes the weather moist and then tempers it in the middle. It causes earthquakes and becomes fiery in the south.

<column-break/>

**Column 2**

**Cancer** brings serenity and heat in parts. In the north, it makes the air moist and cloudy, causing earthquakes, while in the middle, it is tempered. In the south, it is burning and moistens the air, bringing mortality; it then ceases its disturbances.

**Virgo** likewise thunders, heats, and then tempers the air in the middle and the south.

**Libra** likewise tempers the middle and the north. It moves the waters and causes tremors; in the south, it is moist and brings death. It thunders and is fiery.

**Scorpio** makes the air pale and causes movement and winds. In the middle, it is tempered, but in the south, it moistens and brings winds.

**Sagittarius** moistens and is tempered in the middle, but it is fiery and brings winds. In the south, it strongly moistens.

**Capricorn** moistens less; in the middle, it is tempered, but it causes rains. In the south, it strongly moistens and then ceases.

**Aquarius** cools the waters in the north and is moist. In the middle, it is tempered until the end of October. In the south, it causes excessive winds.

**Pisces** causes thunder, cools, and brings tremors. In the north, it is tempered, but in the middle, it strongly moistens. It makes the air pale and brings tremors. In the south, it is aquatic and strongly moistens. These are the general effects through which the months from April onward are influenced.

For those to whom the Moon is joined, certain authors say the **Part of Fortune** <note>original: "partes fortune"; a mathematical point in a birth chart used to predict prosperity</note> and its lord, the lord of the triplicity <note>original: "dñm triũit̃"; one of the three planets that rule a specific element (fire, earth, air, water)</note>, and its second lord and its house, and he who is the ruler over the luminaries <note>The Sun and the Moon</note> at the origin, indicate the fortune of the native. And the reason for this is that the lord of the part in its sign is the cause of prosperity. 

In the ascensions of that place <note>original: "ay sia almpñiz"; likely referring to the rising times of the signs</note>, the Sun in the 6th house <note>Historically considered a "bad" house associated with illness and labor.</note> gives light just as the Moon does; they make this person fortunate in power. The Moon, as the lord, opens the house, and the Part of Fortune is found in misfortune, yet many are fortunate. 

When the Sun and Moon are in their same aspect, many are fortunate. When they behold each other, they are also fortunate. From the treasure of the Sun comes fortune and wealth <note>original: "thezaurizat"; to store up or treasure</note>, even if the planet is the lord of the 12th house <note>The 12th house is usually associated with hidden enemies and loss, showing a complex interpretation here.</note>. 

If the lord aspects thus, as do the Moon and Fortune, the lord of the house of the Part perceives whether it is good or evil. If it does not find its lords, the native shall be in labor without fruit <note>original: "nat g̃ fno ĩ n labore"; meaning working without gaining profit</note>. 

If the lord of the Moon or Fortune is absent, there is no lordship. If the lord of the Moon is in an evil disposition, he seeks it through evil and it shall not last. 

If the luminaries are in the same sign <note>original: "in eodẽ cñ"; a conjunction</note>, the Part of Fortune is in aspect, and he who is born then is fortunate under the power of the lord, because that Part of Fortune is in aspect.

<column-break/>

And he is fortunate because the Part of Fortune is in the midheaven <note>original: "in m°"; likely medium coeli, the highest point of the chart</note>. Fortune is in a constellation of favors. 

From the **Fixed Stars** <note>Stars that do not move like planets (e.g., Regulus or Aldebaran).</note> and from the distance of the planets from the angles, the authors say that even if the species may change, the angles change the manner. The fixed stars give excess, but it is evil for the wise when it is at the end of the bounds. 

Regarding the principle of the years of life, some say 71 or 76 years is the first [limit]. When the status of the hour changes, the multitude of signs and the positions of the planets give to them good or evil. 

If the positions are in the exaltation of the native, like the luminaries, then those born are free and far from misfortune; they are worthy of the principal things and their seed shall inherit the earth. 

From the 10th house <note>The house of career and public standing.</note> and the cadent houses <note>houses 3, 6, 9, and 12, which are considered weaker</note> where there is no grace, such a native suffers evil because no one can be an author except God. For good or for health, let there be light, but for evil or for death, it is as a point of loss.

### Concerning Brothers
Regarding certain houses of brothers: [look to] the lord and the two triplicity lords who act upon this. 

**Brothers** are signified by **Saturn** <note>Usually associated with older brothers or burdens.</note> by day, and by night by **Jupiter** <note>original: "equo"; possibly a scribal error or specific term for the planet of justice/growth</note>. For others, they look to **Mars** and the two triplicity lords, and the lord who aspects them. 

If there is any concord among these, there will be many brothers. If the sign of children has many, then there are many brothers and sisters. 

If the significators <note>The planets representing siblings in the chart.</note> are in a **masculine sign**, they are brothers; if in a **feminine sign**, they are sisters. If the significators aspect each other well, they shall live in concord.

# Concerning Physical Hindrances and Infirmities

The newborn is hindered among <note>original: "natus impeditus inter"; refers to those born with physical disabilities</note>. There are some instances where, if the **significators of children** <note>planets that indicate the fate of one's offspring</note> are well-placed, the children will be safe, and it is rare that they are not a source of joy. 

For those born of women as described, just as the **Lord** <note>the ruling planet of the birth chart</note> girds them, and more than the proper substance, the infant is born according to principal accidents <note>astrological "accidents" are temporary or non-essential conditions</note> while the Lord surrounds it. Unless the Lord is located in a malignant place, specifically if it was in the angle and hindered by waters, the one born in these months will possess this. 

If the **Victor** <note>the Almuten, or most powerful planet in the chart</note> is in that place and appears weak because it is deprived of heat by coldness, the child will be bleary-eyed <note>original: "lippus"</note> or suffer from **gout** <note>original: "podagra"; a painful joint disease often associated with Saturn in medieval medicine</note> and **dropsy** <note>original: "ydropicus"; an accumulation of fluid in the body</note>. 

If **Mars** is present and the "advent" <note>the arrival of a planetary influence</note> appears and hinders the dignity, the whole body will be infirm with **red choler** <note>one of the four humors, associated with heat and anger</note> and a flow of blood. And if the **Part of Fortune** was in these places and appeared above others, it would grant both salvation and infirmity, as well as fortune; and this is because it was "void" <note>original: "vacuum"; likely referring to a "void of course" Moon, which lacks aspects to other planets</note>. So in the first instance, let it be noted that the influence is inseparable from the anger <note>original: "hira," likely *ira*</note> in which the Lord remains in the eighth house <note>the house of death and hidden things</note>.

In the signs governing the limbs, those born may be hindered in some member <note>limb or part of the body</note> as stated before. When the **Moon** appears in such an aspect, there was a hindrance from an evil part. If the sign in which the Moon resided was in the **left eye**, it is changed from its proper mode. 

When there is a "Lunar" condition which is as a prediction of evil in the second aspect of fire <note>referring to the Fiery Triplicity: Aries, Leo, Sagittarius</note>, so that it foresees and the aspect of the malifics <note>Saturn and Mars</note> is seen, the newborn appears with a wide opening of the eyes <note>original: "rictu octor' [oculorum]"</note> and the whites are affected, provided the Moon is thrice hindered by the opposition and appearance of the malifics.

<column-break/>

And in no way are they appended from the signs of choler, nor does **Fortune** appear through the eyes when the Moon is hindered. In the second sign, without the aforementioned prediction of the stronger planets <note>original: "vadior," possibly *validiorum*</note>, Fortune leads to dropsy. The limbs of the newborn are governed by the sign of Mars, which causes differences in how the hindrances manifest. 

When the **Moon** is in the eyes <note>meaning in an astrological degree associated with sight</note>, such as in the hollow of **Leo**, or by the influence of fire or water, it signifies a hindrance of the eyes. This may cause the onset of eye trouble for the newborn, or he may be afflicted by **elephantiasis** <note>a severe skin and tissue disease</note>, **white leprosy**, **gout**, **cancer**, and evils of the throat. 

When the **Moon** is in its own signs or influenced by **Saturn** <note>abbreviated as "le," likely *leone* or a shorthand for Saturn</note> or **Mars** in the eighth house, or in opposite appearance, the newborn is corrupted by various afflictions. The **Part of Fortune** prefigures the "binding" <note>original: "abp̃di," likely *abpendi* or *alligari*</note> of the newborn's eyes. If the planets are in their own dignities, they are strong and apt; if they are weak, add labor and affliction with infirmity. 

In "beastly" signs <note>signs represented by animals, like Aries, Taurus, Leo</note>, the binding occurs in the morning. This affects the solar veins in the left side. When the **Moon** is the primary cause of the sickness, and if the fire of Mars was malignant in the "root" <note>the original birth chart</note>, the illness is grave. When the stars are infirm and the signs are heavy, the newborn's limbs will be affected. <term>☿</term> **Mercury** and <term>♃</term> **Jupiter** may provide some protection there.

**Saturn** preceding the eyes in a malignant way is not saved by the meridian. The evils which are "accidental" <note>secondary astrological influences</note> bring diseases that must be respected. When the **Moon** is afflicted, it brings forth an onset of illness. If **Mars** was in the sign of blood at the moment the child was born, there will be issues of the blood.

# On the Timing of Medicines and Surgery

For this reason, one must consider with less haste how [the patient's] generation occurred, and from which planetary slips <note>original: "p̄lap⁹"; refers to the accidental positions or "falls" of planets</note> a corruption or an appearance [of illness] arises. This is determined according to the proportions and the **zodiac signs**. One can better understand this through the **Moon's cycle** <note>original: "luazıū"; the lunar month or phase</note> and through the influence of both the good and the malevolent planets.

If in any way the Moon appears joined with **Jupiter** <note>reconstructed from "ıone"</note>, the work will be effective; however, if it is joined with a malevolent planet, the effect is diminished. 

### Guidelines for Purgatives and Emetics

Take a **purgative medicine** <note>original: "purgatorıū"; a treatment to cleanse the bowels of "corrupt humors"</note> when the Moon is in a certain time <note>likely waxing or waning depending on the humor being treated</note> and when the two planets with virtue are below the horizon, which is a laudable time. If, however, you must take an **emetic** <note>original: "vomıt medıuaz"; medicine to induce vomiting</note>, do so when the Moon is positioned with planets above the earth.

### Surgical Warnings

One must never touch a limb with **iron** <note>original: "ferro"; meaning surgical instruments like scalpels or lancets</note> when the Moon is in the zodiac sign that governs that specific limb. For example, do not perform surgery on the arms <note>governed by Gemini</note> when the Moon is in that sign. Furthermore, you should not perform **bloodletting** <note>original: "mınuı aas" / "minutio sanguinis"</note> when the Moon is in **Leo**, in the **Tail of the Dragon** <note>the South Node of the Moon, considered malefic</note>, or when the Moon is in **Scorpio**.

### On Critical Days and Disease

Two things must be inspected: the position of the Moon and the relationship between the physician and the sick man. The hours in which the disease becomes clearer, whether for good or for bad, are determined by the location of the Moon in **quadrature** <note>original: "ı̄ q̄ dratıs"; a 90-degree square aspect</note> or other configurations, such as the **orthogonal** <note>right-angle</note> aspect, or the **trine** <note>120-degree aspect</note>. These determine the "critical days" <note>original: "dıes vıvıs" / "dies critici"</note>—the days when a disease reaches its turning point. These cycles can also bring about visions or intense pain if the Moon does not dominate the humor properly. Consider the fifth day especially...

<column-break/>

...in an angle, so that it occurs in a ray or in opposition. This strengthens the infirmities as if they were bound by the figure and locations of the stars. The stars resonate with the body through the **Ascendant** <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> and the lunar power.

### The Governance of the Body (Melothesia)

The various parts of the body and the senses are attributed to the stars as follows:

*   **Aries** governs the head and those things pertaining to the face and full vision.
*   The **Lungs** and the **Heart** <note>original: "pulıııonē coııdııı"</note> are influenced by the Sun and **Mars**.
*   The **Sun** <note>original: "Sol"</note> governs the eyes and the vital spirit.
*   **Venus** governs the sense of smell and the **liver** <note>original: "epaz" / "hepar"</note>.
*   **Mercury** governs the tongue, the power of speech, and the **memory**.
*   The **Sun**, by its nature, also governs the sense of taste and the vital heat.

These triple <note>original: "Trıpte"</note> powers—the vital, the natural, and the animal—flow from these celestial sources. When the Moon is in conjunction or in a difficult aspect with other stars, the physician must be careful. For example, if a star appears in a certain figure, the lunar medicine <note>original: "pııc lııofa"</note> which is... <unclear>aliforaze</unclear>...

# The Influence of the Heavens on the Body's Form

And the spirit [is influenced by] the **Tail of the Archer** <note>original: "sagitte canda"; refers to the stars in the tail of Sagittarius</note>. For this reason, one must consider what occurs around the tail. For those desiring [to understand] the influence of **Leo** <note>the zodiac sign the Lion</note>, and those things arising from the Moon and the malevolent planets...

When the Moon falls with **Mars** or the **Sun**, or rises with them in fate, and the Moon moves toward the Archer <note>original: "carp"; likely referring to Capricorn or the Archer's bow</note>. If the Sun was in any **angle** <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the most powerful points in a horoscope</note> and with the Lion, these two positions should be closely watched. Or if two [planets] are in the **loins** <note>the part of the body governed by Libra</note> in that region, it signifies death; and in the same sign or in the opposites, a disease will be seen to hinder the person.

**Mars** causes a blow or strike and produces an infirmity such as **jaundice** <note>original: "gigeri lutea"; literally yellow-illness, likely referring to the yellowing of the skin or eyes</note>. **Saturn** causes **albugo** <note>original: "albugine oculorz"; white spots or cataracts in the eyes</note>, or cold humors, or a **ranula** <note>original: "ranularue"; a cyst under the tongue named for its frog-like appearance</note> or similar ailments of the throat and eyes. When a planet is elevated in the center, or if it is opposed, earlier deformations occur in the part of the body that the sign rules, including the head.

And if the Moon is with the **mute signs** <note>original: "mute habiti"; the water signs Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces, which were thought to cause speech impediments</note> while the Sun rises from the east, it makes men **mute** <note>original: "murt"; silent or unable to speak</note>. If a planet is elevated above them or opposed, they remain without resonance, as if closed off. And if the sound of the Sun is in that part of the signs, the more the Moon passes through them strongly, the more a defect will accumulate, such as an impediment of the testicles or a man born under the **Lion** having a distorted body as if he were in the water. If there is theft or passion, he will not escape some onset of eye disease.

<column-break/>

**Saturn**, or when joined with the **Sun**, will cause an impediment and a murmur [of the voice] if the Moon is associated with it in a sign; never will the thinness of the tongue be absent, and it will be mostly bare. Behold the measured stars in an angle; if they are unfortunate, or if they are in opposition to the luminaries [the Sun and Moon], it will cause bad things in two ways.

The **Node** <note>original: "moasmon"; a corruption of 'Anabibazon' or similar term for the lunar nodes</note>, which is the **Head and Tail of the Dragon**, leads to infirmities in the signs such as being **hunchbacked** <note>original: "gibbosus"</note>, or having some part of the body destroyed, or being **lame** <note>original: "claudy"</note> as if the limb were dislocated. And if the luminaries are situated in this way, even for a man of noble birth, if a malevolent planet is elevated above the luminaries through an opposition or from its own angles in a **square aspect** <note>original: "p quadratum"; an astrological aspect of 90 degrees, usually considered difficult</note>.

If **Mars** is elevated to lead, it brings the heat of fire or major burns. If it should happen to be in certain points, it causes **morphea** <note>original: "morphea"; localized skin discoloration or hardening</note>, that is, white spots. Truly, under the **Sun**, there arise skin eruptions like **impetigo** <note>original: "impetigies"</note> and **albaras** <note>original: "albarad"; a term from Arabic medicine for white leprosy or vitiligo</note>, which are spots that sink deep toward the bone. 

Under the **Sun**, pits and scabby spots are created when it is associated with malevolent planets. **Saturn** truly causes shadowy spots and stains the body with morbidity; it brings the plague of **leprosy** <note>original: "leprax"</note> and the pain of an ulcer when it first appears, filled with blood and moved by the "combustion" of **melancholy** <note>original: "melanio adustioe"; the black bile humor becoming "burnt" or toxic</note>. This manifests in the eyes and limbs, and it is said to lead from the ear to the palate and the stomach.

# On the Fatality of Illness and the Moon

<column-break/>

They apply <note>term: "application"; an astrological event where a faster-moving planet approaches a specific angle or "aspect" with a slower one, indicating an upcoming event.</note> it is fatal, and if the Moon is in its highest point <note>original: "aux"; the apogee, where a planet's influence was thought to be most refined or distant.</note>, it leads to corruption. To whatever the Moon responds, it is either a falling away or a "combustion" <note>term: "combustion"; when a planet is so close to the Sun—within 8.5 degrees—that its power is "burned up" or hidden.</note>; that combustion provides a mortal warning. If she is in a degree that alleviates the disease, the state of the mind remains firm. All these diseases are signified when they do not finish.

### Concerning the 12th House

<meta>This page serves as the formal opening of the text. It transitions from the general introductory apparatus to the specific preface by Alchabitius (Al-Qabisi), followed by a table of contents for the "Differences" (chapters) and the beginning of the technical description of the Zodiac.</meta>

# Here begins the introductory book of Alchabitius toward mastery in the judgment of the stars

Having requested from the Lord a long life, and that the sword of kings be turned away, and for the protection of their wealth and honors, as well as the extension of their kingdom—that which is healthy to recount as having been seen—it is known that certain ancients among the authors of the <term>mastery of the judgment of the stars<note>original: "magisterij iudiciorz astrorum"; this refers to judicial astrology, the art of predicting events based on celestial movements.</note></term> published books which they called "Introductions" to this kind of mastery and judgment of the stars. But some among them were not diligent, omitting things that should have been in their proper order in their teachings, while others—whom it is not our place to name—produced their works with such great length that they grew tedious to the mind. Indeed, some who speculated on the judgments of these matters did not apply themselves to the study of doctrine or the computation of discipline. Therefore, I have sought to publish this book and have placed it as an introduction and collection for my colleagues, providing certain things from our <term>mastery<note>original: "magisteris"; the specialized craft of the astrologer.</note></term> by way of an introduction, and not just an introduction but a rational arrangement or distribution of those things which, though few, are of great price. This work is called *The Introduction* by <note>The text here likely refers to the author's name, Abd al-Aziz (Alchabitius).</note> Al-Qabisi, in which I have treated those things which I have put forth for the confirmation of the mastery of the judgment of the stars.

<column-break/>

It is called [the Introduction], and in it is the destruction of the letters <gloss>Sahl ibn Bishr in his introduction regarding them<note>original: "sehalach in amchila"; refers to the 9th-century astrologer Sahl ibn Bishr, a primary source for this text.</note></gloss> with the agreement of those who were able to be there. And I have divided it into five <term>Differences<note>original: "differentias"; used here to mean chapters or distinct sections of the treatise.</note></term>:
The **First Difference** is on the essentials <unclear>and the signs</unclear>. (Page 113)
The **Second Difference** is on the nature of the planets and their properties, and what they signify of themselves. (Page 118)
The **Third Difference** is on the accidents that happen to the planets in themselves and the accidents involving each other. (Page 181)
The **Fourth Difference** is on the <note>Commonly refers to the "parts" or lots used in astrology.</note> names used by astrologers. (Page 188)
The **Fifth Difference** is on the "will" of the planets and the composition of their effects in the degrees.

<margin>Division of the Zodiac</margin>

# The Zodiac is therefore divided into 12 equal parts according to the division of the circle of signs, and these are specifically called "signs." They refer to the images that are under that same circle of the Zodiac, and they are: **Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, and Pisces.** And each of these parts of the signs is divided into 30 equal parts which are called **degrees**; and a degree into 60 **minutes**; and a minute into 60 **seconds**; and a second into 60 **thirds**; and a third into 60 **fourths**; and so extending by the order of descent unto infinity <note>The author explains the sexagesimal (base-60) system used in astronomical coordinates.</note>. Furthermore, some of the signs are **Northern**, that is, from the beginning of Aries until the end of Virgo, according to the equatorial line; and others are **Southern**, that is, from the beginning of Libra until the end of Pisces. These are what the ancients say...

<meta>This page continues the technical introduction to astrology by Al-Qabisi (Alchabitius), moving from the general definitions of the signs to their specific astronomical properties—such as how they rise over the horizon—and their relationship to the seasons, the human body, and the stages of life.</meta>

### Concerning the Parts

<column-break/>

<margin>Signs that are seen as straight</margin>
The <term>right-ascending signs<note>original: "Signa recte"; these are signs that take longer to rise over the horizon in the northern hemisphere, appearing to rise more "upright."</note></term> ascend, for example, from the beginning of <term>Cancer<note>The Crab</note></term> until the end of <term>Sagittarius<note>The Archer</note></term>.
<margin>Signs that are seen as crooked</margin>
The directly opposite signs, which ascend "crookedly" or <term>obliquely<note>original: "tortuose"; these signs take less time to rise and appear to "slant" across the horizon.</note></term>, ascend, for example, from the beginning of <term>Capricorn<note>The Sea-Goat</note></term> to the end of <term>Gemini<note>The Twins</note></term>. These obliquely ascending signs are said to "obey" the directly ascending ones.
<term>And</term> <term>Note</term> that signs which are of the same distance from the "head" (start) of <term>Aries<note>The Ram</note></term> or from the line of the <term>mid-heaven<note>original: "medij celi"; the highest point the sun reaches in the sky.</note></term> obey one another, such as <term>Gemini</term> and <term>Cancer</term>, <term>Leo</term> and <term>Virgo</term>, <term>Aries</term> and <term>Taurus</term>, or <term>Libra</term>, <term>Scorpio</term>, and <term>Sagittarius</term>. <term>And</term> two signs which are of the same distance from the start

of Aries are said to be <term>concordant<note>original: "concordantia"; signs that share the same power or light because they are equidistant from the equinoxes.</note></term>, and they "see" each other, just as <term>Pisces</term> and <term>Taurus</term>, <term>Aquarius</term> and <term>Gemini</term>, <term>Capricorn</term> and <term>Cancer</term>, <term>Sagittarius</term> and <term>Leo</term>, or <term>Scorpio</term>, <term>Virgo</term>, and <term>Libra</term>.

Summary of the First Part concerning the Planets

# Concerning the Wandering Stars
Among all the <term>wandering stars<note>original: "stellis erraticis"; the ancient term for the planets, which appeared to "wander" against the fixed background of the stars.</note></term> which are moved under the <term>vault of heaven<note>original: "sub ligno uis"; likely a scribal or OCR error for "sub limite" or "sub linea," referring to the planetary spheres.</note></term>, we find that they are distinguished by their height and the speed of their movement. The highest of them, and the one with the slowest course, is **Saturn**. Then, below him, is **Mars**; next is the **Sun**; then **Venus**; then **Mercury**; and the lowest is the **Moon**, which is closest to the Earth and moves more swiftly than all the others. The <term>Head of the Dragon<note>original: "Caput draconis"; the ascending node where the Moon crosses the ecliptic northward.</note></term> and the **Tail** are also noted in the charts. Certain significations are joined together in the <term>scepters<note>original: "scēptis"; likely a reference to planetary "powers" or "rulers."</note></term> that the planets hold in these signs, which provide certain <term>privileges<note>original: "p̄ūāz"; an abbreviation for "praerogativas" or "privilegia."</note></term>. These privileges are as follows: **House**, **Exaltation**, **Triplicity**, **Term**, and **Face**. We shall now attempt to describe those which occur. The **House** <note>original: "Domus"; the sign where a planet is most "at home" and powerful.</note> of **Aries** and **Scorpio** is the lordship of **Mars**; **Taurus** and **Libra** are the houses of **Venus**; **Gemini** and **Virgo** are the houses of **Mercury**; **Cancer** is the house of the **Moon**; **Leo** is the house of the **Sun**; **Sagittarius** and **Pisces** are the lordship of **Jupiter**; and **Capricorn** and **Aquarius** are the houses of **Saturn**. It should be known that although a sign belongs to the whole universe, it serves as the <term>foundation<note>original: "dēmen tū"; likely "fundamentum."</note></term> for the planet. Those two signs which are the houses of the planets are said to be their <term>chief dwellings<note>original: "gc̄or di na"; possibly "gradus ordinarii."</note></term>. In the middle of the zodiac's course, certain signs are those in which the planets are said to **rejoice** <margin>rejoices</margin>. According to the tradition of Dorotheus <note>Dorotheus of Sidon, a 1st-century astrological poet.</note>, it is established that the lords move toward their joy: **Saturn** rejoices in **Aquarius**; **Jupiter** in **Sagittarius**; **Mars** in **Scorpio**; 

<column-break/>

**Venus** in **Libra**; and **Mercury** in **Virgo**.
<margin>Joys of the planets</margin>
The **Sun** is **exalted** <note>original: "exaltat̄"; a position of great strength, second only to its House.</note> in **Aries**, specifically in its 19th degree; the **Moon** in the 3rd degree of **Taurus**; **Saturn** in the 21st degree of **Libra**; **Jupiter** in the 15th degree of **Cancer**; **Mars** in the 28th degree of **Capricorn**; **Venus** in the 21st degree of **Pisces**; **Mercury** in the 15th degree of **Virgo**; the **Head of the Dragon** in the 3rd degree of **Gemini**; and the **Tail** in the 3rd degree of **Sagittarius**. In the signs directly opposite these exaltations, the planets are said to be in their **fall** <note>original: "casus"; the position where a planet's influence is most weakened.</note>. For example, if the Sun is exalted in the 19th degree of Aries, it falls in the 19th degree of Libra. However, **Ptolemy** <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century astronomer.</note> places the whole of Aries as the Sun's exaltation and the whole of Taurus as the Moon's exaltation.

<margin>Triplicities</margin>

# Concerning the Triplicities
We distinguish the **Triplicities** next, for three signs which are seen to agree in one nature are joined together and called a "triplicity" by the same name. For instance, **Aries**, **Leo**, and **Sagittarius** <margin>Triplicity</margin> make the **first triplicity** because each of these signs is masculine, fiery, and shares a bitter taste.

And let one look toward the middle so that they are joined, whether by a <term>sextile<note>original: "sextili"; an aspect where planets are 60 degrees apart, considered moderately harmonious.</note></term>, or by a <term>square<note>original: "quadr"; also known as a quadrate, an aspect of 90 degrees, often considered a position of tension.</note></term>. And there is a just aspect called a <term>trine<note>original: "trigono"; an aspect where planets are 120 degrees apart (one-third of the circle).</note></term>, or I see it as trigonal, which occupies 120 parts <note>degrees</note> of the heaven. And thus, concerning the aspect of harmony and perfect love, let it also look from the seventh sign, which is the <term>opposition<note>original: "opposito"; an aspect of 180 degrees where planets are directly across from one another.</note></term>; this is the aspect of contradiction, discord, and perfect enmity. Similarly, it is pleasing for the signs to look upon each other in this way. While they look at each other—that is, when they "aspect"—if two planets are joined in one sign, these two <term>planets<note>original: "placeta," likely a scribe's variation of "planeta."</note></term> are in conjunction. When they are in other signs, a planet emits its rays into those signs that look upon it through a "useless" sign <note>A sign that does not form a major aspect is sometimes called "inconjunct" or "disconnected."</note>. For example: If one planet is in the first degree of **Aries** and another is in the 7th sign <note>Libra</note>, then its rays will be in the first degree of **Libra**, and in the first degree of the same; understand the other aspects in this same way. Furthermore, an aspect following the succession of the signs is called "sinister" <note>left-handed</note>, directed toward the first degree of the succession of signs. Regarding the "dexter" <note>right-handed</note> aspect, it occurs backward, rather than sinister.

Through every sign, the division of the zodiac is made by minutes and quantities, distributed as a moderate body so that the work would not be too long.

### On the Faces of the Signs

<margin>
Face 1
Face 2
Face 3
</margin>
The <term>faces<note>original: "facies"; also known as "decans," these are 10-degree subdivisions of a zodiac sign. Each sign has three faces.</note></term> of the signs are as follows: each of the signs is divided into 3 equal parts, each of which consists of 10 <term>degrees<note>original: "gradibus"</note></term>, and they are called "faces." The first face is from the beginning of the sign. Therefore, the first face is from the first degree of the said sign up to the 10th, and it is given to **Mars**. The second [face] starts from the end [of the first] up to the 20th degree and is given to the **Sun**, who follows him in the order of the heavens. The third is from the 20th up to the end of the aforementioned sign, and finally, the first face of the next sign is given to **Venus**, who follows the Sun; and so it continues until the end of the signs.

<margin>On the method of the aforementioned faces</margin>
There are therefore lines which are drawn in other signs according to this example. The faces are [calculated] from the degrees of the said sign up to the sign of which the face is sought. Thus, you should triple the number of signs, and if there are any remaining degrees above the parts, they are distributed from those faces of the signs. One is always in the same face when the calculation is turned. Here the rule is provoked <note>This section describes a mathematical formula for calculating which planet rules a specific degree.</note> as in the first face, which is from Mars because he is the lord of the first face of the sign **Aries**. And through his influence, the planet finishes there. And that face, which the sign concludes, finishes at that part where the sign itself ends. One must follow the faces of the other planets according to the sequence. For example, by way of the path, if the face is to be found for a certain degree, you count the signs from **Aries** up to that point.

<column-break/>

To this sum, you add the faces of the figures and the degrees of the face until the piety <note>likely "quantity" or "totality"</note> of the face is completed. And there are in this proposal 2 faces. In this way, you then divide the sum by 7, and the remainder shows which planet rules. For example, if the remainder is 5, it is in the face of **Venus**, who is the third from **Mars** according to the order of the planets. And the following faces, namely the 3 faces of the house under the lordship of **Mercury**, and so understand the others. Or other signs through their own numbers and proportions. Regarding that which remains, you distribute it through the planets according to their order, beginning from **Mars**. You will find the planet in the lordship or the dignity. The face of the last sign follows the same sequence of planets, following the lord of the previous face of the sign, namely the lord of the face. Consider therefore the middle of the face, whatever the lord may be, and you will recognize its influence. There follows a description of these:

### On the strengths of the
### planets according to the signs

But because, dear friend, enough has already been said concerning the parts of the noble planets and their **houses**, **exaltations**, **triplicities**, and indeed their **faces**, we must now speak of their strengths in those natural houses attributed to them. Understand, therefore, that the value for the strengths of the planets—whereby one planet abounds more in strength than another—is as follows: [attributing to the] lord of the house [five?], to the lord of the <term>exaltation<note>original: "exaltationi"; a sign where a planet's influence is particularly powerful, second only to its own house.</note></term> [four], to the lord of the <term>triplicity<note>original: "triplicitatis"; a group of three signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water).</note></term> three, to the lord of the <term>terms<note>original: "termini"; unequal subdivisions of a sign where specific planets hold power.</note></term> two, and to the lord of the <term>faces<note>original: "facierum"; 10-degree subdivisions, also called decans.</note></term> one. And some indeed assign four to the triplicity, as he wished that the lord of the terms be stronger than the lord of the triplicity through the method explained above on folio 12v, namely assigning 4 to each.

<margin>1/3 i</margin>
The second [view] on this matter is spoken of by the experts, who say that when a planet is in its own **house**, it is to be seen [as having] two [strengths] of its own; and when it is in its **exaltation**, it has 3 volumes of its own glory; and when it is in its **terms**, it is like a master among his parents and kinsmen; and in its **triplicity**, it is like a man of honor among his helpers and ministers; and when it is in its **face**, it is as if it were in its own images. These are all the essential parts of the planets in the signs.

<margin>4</margin>
Now concerning the signs that are figured [depicted]: they call some "rational" or "human," namely **Virgo**, **Gemini**, **Libra**, **Aquarius**, and the middle part of **Sagittarius**, because the images of these are like males, or the images are figured as humans; therefore, these are called rational figures.

<column-break/>

<margin>a beautiful voice</margin>
You call these [signs] human, and in them flourishes [the quality of voice], just as in the sciences <margin>eloquence</margin>. And some call others [different names], namely **Gemini**, **Virgo**, and **Pisces**. <margin>Note</margin> <margin>Demostria</margin> And some are "quadrupedal" [four-legged], such as **Leo** and **Sagittarius** (in its body), <margin>vigor</margin> while others are contrary, namely **Aries**, **Taurus**, and **Capricorn**; and then [this quality] flourishes when it is in the middle... and **Aquarius** flourishes at the end in perfection. -> **Distinction** <-

In each sign below, [the author] has treated the signs themselves. If, after the planets [pass] through the signs, someone manifests a clear meaning regarding pain in the human limbs, the signs signify it. First, concerning **Aries**: <margin>♈︎</margin> In **Aries**, **Saturn** governs the feet and the upper belly; **Mars** governs the head; the **Sun** governs the thighs; **Venus** governs the feet and hands; **Mercury** <note>original: "aura"; likely a corruption of "aures"</note> governs the ears; and the **Moon** governs the knees.

In **Taurus**: <margin>♉︎</margin> **Saturn** governs the upper back; **Mars** the necks; the **Sun** the knees; **Venus** the head, hands, and feet; the **Moon** the ears.

In **Gemini**: <margin>♊︎</margin> **Saturn** governs the upper genitals and whatever parts fall below them; **Mars** the chest; the **Sun** the ears and <term>armpits<note>original: "amillas"; a corruption of the Latin "axillas."</note></term>; **Venus** the necks, hands, and head; the **Moon** the feet.

In **Cancer**: <margin>♋︎</margin> **Saturn** governs the navel and those parts below it, as well as the upper thighs; **Mars** the chest; the **Sun** the feet; **Venus** the arms and shoulders; **Mercury** the eyes; the **Moon** the head.

In **Leo**: <margin>♌︎</margin> **Saturn** governs the genitals and their surrounding parts, including the upper thighs and knees; **Mars** the chest; the **Sun** the head; **Venus** the heart, navel, shoulders, and throat; the **Moon** the neck.

In **Virgo**: <margin>♍︎</margin> **Saturn** governs the feet, knees, and their surrounding parts; **Mars** the belly; the **Sun** the neck; **Venus** the belly, hands, and heart; the **Moon** the shoulders.

In **Libra**: <margin>♎︎</margin> **Saturn** governs the knees and their surrounding parts, and the upper eyes; **Mars** the genitals and the lower body; the **Sun** the shoulders; **Venus** the head, hands, and belly; the **Moon** the heart.

In **Scorpio**: <margin>♏︎</margin> **Saturn** governs the <term>armpits<note>original: "camillas"; likely another corruption of "axillas."</note></term> and their surroundings, and the feet; **Mars** the arms, head, and thighs;

<column-break/>

the **Sun** governs the heart or genitals and their surrounding parts; **Venus** the genitals and those parts which follow, as well as the hands and back; the **Moon** the belly.

In **Sagittarius**: <margin>♐︎</margin> **Saturn** governs the feet, ears, and head; **Mars** the hands and feet; the **Sun** the belly; **Venus** the thighs, arms, hands, genitals, and heart; the **Moon** the back.

In **Capricorn**: <margin>♑︎</margin> **Saturn** governs the head and feet, knees, and eyes; **Mars** the ears and shoulders; the **Sun** the back; **Venus** the thighs and heart; [Mercury/Mars] <note>The text is ambiguous here but refers to the remaining planetary power</note> the hands, genitals, and their surrounding parts; the **Moon** the thighs and other parts following the heart.

In **Aquarius**: <margin>♒︎</margin> **Saturn** governs the head and neck, upper shoulders, and feet, and partly the limbs, armpits, and heart; the **Sun** the genitals and the lower body; **Venus** the knees and their surroundings, the hands, thighs, and heart; the **Moon** the genitals.

In **Pisces**: <margin>♓︎</margin> **Saturn** governs the shoulders, arms, and neck, heart and chest, armpits and belly; the **Sun** the thighs and the lower body; **Venus** the <unclear>rollum</unclear> and back <unclear>nitingum</unclear> and genitals; the **Moon** the <unclear>foia</unclear> <note>original: "foia"; possibly "fovea" (hollows of the body) or "femora" (thighs).</note>.

# Concerning the Divisions

There are also certain modules—one might call them **increments of fortune**—and these are: in **Aries** 19, in **Taurus** 14, in **Gemini** 11, and in **Sagittarius** [no value].

->[Image: A circular diagram showing the twelve zodiac signs with their associated degrees. The vertical line is marked as the "Ascendant."]<-

And for two degrees that have an equal length, take the two corresponding noble signs, in all their customary strengths and princes in power. For example: the 20th degree of **Capricorn** or **Aquarius** with the 10th degree of **Sagittarius** and **Gemini**; and the 20th degree of **Aries** and **Libra** with the 10th degree of **Pisces** and **Virgo**.

->[Image: A second circular diagram repeating the twelve signs, illustrating the geometric relationships and degrees described in the text.]<-

<margin>On the twelve houses</margin>
And because the providence of the gods has provided for this expansion, just as there is effectiveness in the figures for bringing forth and approaching the path of every good thing... such a figure is divided into equal parts. This is done by the circle of the hemisphere, which creates the midday point <note>This refers to the meridian or Midheaven</note>. Each of these is further divided into three unequal parts according to the aspect, as the sign ascends. This divides the whole circle into twelve parts. These are named **"houses"** <note>original: domus</note>, though they are also called **"courts"** <note>original: curiae</note> and the **"cusps of the angles."** This is explained more fully in the *Book of Canons* <note>original: libro canonum</note> and in the *Book on the Course of the Stars* <note>original: libro de cursu siderum</note>.

The specific distinction of these is the <term>Ascendant<gloss>The sign or degree of the zodiac rising over the eastern horizon at a specific moment.</gloss></term> <note>original: ascendens</note> angle, located above the circle of the eastern hemisphere. Then the 2nd follows, then the 9th, then the 3rd, and so on up to the 12th.

<margin>According to the spoken traditions of the sphere...</margin>
The fourth part, stretching from the Ascendant up to the <term>Midheaven<gloss>The highest point in the sky at the time of birth, representing one's public life and career.</gloss></term> <note>original: medium celi</note>—which comprises houses 12, 11, and 10—is said to be general and masculine. It pertains to youth and signifies the nature of life and the entire span <note>original: sagenam, literally "fishing net" or "enclosure"</note> of childhood.

And the other part, which is from the Midheaven to the West <note>The Descendant</note>...

<margin>The fourth [part] is the feminine half</margin>
...comprising signs 7, 8, and 9, which is above the circle of the western hemisphere. This is called the second part, and it is masculine according to Maderus <note>Possibly a reference to the 4th-century astrologer Firmicus Maternus</note>. It pertains to the middle age of life and the perfection of the world... [then melancholy].

The third part, which is from the West to the <term>Bottom of the Sky<gloss>The lowest point of the chart, representing the northern sky below the horizon; often associated with home, roots, and the end of life.</gloss></term> <note>original: imum celi</note>, which is above the circle of the midheaven described as being beneath the earth...

At the ascendant, the quadrant is northern and feminine; it governs the "nights" <note>night-time or hidden matters</note> and what happens to a man after death—what becomes of his body or his legacy, and what is said of him, whether in praise or blame. It also concerns whether he left behind a "flowering seed" or a defect of winter <note>metaphor for legacy or lack thereof</note>. Furthermore, there are two parts before the horizon up to the ascendant, and from the ascendant up to the **fourth house**.

The second lord of the triplicity <note>term: triplicity; a group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element</note> governs life, the body, and its strength or vigor. The third lord of the triplicity signifies what is outside the self and the end of the person's life.

The **second house** is the **house of hope** and of substance <note>wealth and possessions</note>. It shows the sustenance of the person's life until the end. The master **Alendegor** says of this house that if its lords—the second and third—are in a favorable place, the person will be an author of hope and a significator of wealth... for if they are in the **Midheaven**, he shall find great favor; and if they are in the **house of faith**, it shall be even better. Regarding the lords of the triplicity: the first gives substance in the beginning of life, the second in the middle, and the third at the end.

The **third house** is the house of **brothers and sisters**, of beloved neighbors, of faith and religious commands, of legates, messengers, and kin; it concerns the state of one's life...

## Saturn
He is **masculine**, **malefic** <note>original: "malus," literally "bad," referring to the planet's traditionally challenging influence</note>, and **diurnal**. He signifies the first things <note>possibly referring to the father or early life</note> if the birth was at night, through old age; and he has [this influence] if he was oriental <note>rising before the Sun</note>. His bodily complexion is an increase of melancholy <note>one of the four humors, associated with black bile and a somber temperament</note> and dissolution; or perhaps he is cold, humid, and gouty <note>original: "podagrosa," relating to gout or joint pains</note>. He is of much conversation... and because of his depth, he signifies sons, silence, and the accumulation of aquatic things, as well as the cultivation of fields and of peoples.

<meta>This page continues the detailed description of the nature and influences of the planet Saturn, specifically outlining his psychological effects, the types of wealth he governs, the illnesses he causes, and how his influence changes when combined with other planets. It concludes with a physiognomical description of the "Saturnine" person.</meta>

Triste, gloomy, and prone to ill suspicion and envy; a person who suspects their masters will hold onto their things. <note>original: "male suspicionis et inuidie"</note> If Saturn is well-placed, he will grant some measure of substance and wealth, and the divinity of these things will hold here, etc. But if he is poorly-placed <term>malo: refers to a planet being 'malefic' or in a poor celestial position</term>, he signifies dirty and foul-tasting waters, old things, and those that are decaying. He causes phlegmatic diseases <note>referring to an excess of 'phlegm' in the four humors theory</note>, chronic and multifaceted illnesses, muteness, "dog-leprosy" <note>likely a term for severe scabies or scaly skin diseases</note>, and the like. He also signifies long-distance travels characterized by labor, slowness, affliction, the loss of property, and lawsuits involving the dead. He represents grandfathers, older fathers-in-law, and all lowly and common men; he also signifies their labor and operations. 

If Saturn is alone and without the influence of any other planet, he acts as described. # Regarding the Lordship of the World

Which is not because he has days in the days and nights in the nights; it should be said that his **lordship of the world** <note>original: "dominatum mundi"</note> was placed through his influence, but rather through the greatness of the soul of the wondrous and the good. His strength is multiplied when he is in the north. And some have said that in the bounds from the middle of his **retrogradation** <note>The apparent backward motion of a planet in the sky, usually considered a time of weakened or inverted influence.</note> until his second station, on account of the points... from that state, on account of being joined with the **Sun**, he signifies **youth**; from there until the first station, **middle age**; and from there until the middle of his retrogradation, **old age**. 

Thus, from the middle of his retrogradation until the second station, he represents old age, quietude, and constancy. According to his placement, he shapes the generation of bodies and their **color** and their size. When led by the Sun, he represents [skill] and friendship; then toward the first parts, he represents [skill] and changed love. If his aspect is from the first retrogradation to the second, all things are confused, disjointed, and marked by envy; and he brings comparison in things. In the middle of the "dragons" <note>original: "daconum," likely referring to the lunar nodes known as the Dragon's Head and Tail.</note> there was nobility in peace on account of his ingenuity; or weakness in justice. If there is a comparison in talents and slowness... without reality and scatterings... by his merit with the Sun through the retrograde path, he signifies **happiness** and the comprehension of groans and **robbery**.

<column-break/>

Such a body hears what is spoken and pleases those in palaces. And I say his mind figures the world from the appearance of men: they are not very white nor black in color; they have a slanted forehead, a **long face**, and a **long nose**, with a **sparse beard** on the jaws. The eyes are beautiful, not entirely black. He speaks worthily of his own affairs. He holds the portion of **business** and signifies [upheaval] and infestation, **war**, and enmities; in justice, he signifies the works of the hands. In retrogradation, whether they be in herbs, they say the heart is entirely [troubled]...

### The Moon

The **Moon** is a **feminine fortune** <note>original: "fortuna femia." In traditional astrology, the Moon is considered a beneficial influence, specifically associated with feminine qualities.</note>. She spreads **moisture** and **coldness**. She signifies **mothers**; if she is [well-placed], she is like a night owl. In her is the [highest] sphere, and she was spoken of through justice. And now it is shown from these works: she signifies **embassies** and mandates, especially in lands, according to the quantity of fortune she holds; for if they are good, they are good according to the word. 

She signifies **principalities**; if the Moon is proficient for any in affairs, they pertain to **kings**, provided she was fortunate, in a good aspect, and in a good place relative to the Sun. She signifies **silver** and thin earth. If she was in the **eighth house** <note>The astrological house associated with death, transformation, and shared resources; the Moon here might indicate diminished strength.</note>, her quantity is diminished and her color is more sluggish. ...and this joining is called a conjunction of longitude. <margin>Conjunction of latitude</margin> **Conjunction of latitude** is when two planets are joined in latitude so that they are in one sign and their bodies are equal in height relative to one side; or, if they are opposite, so that the latitude of the body flows equally according to these modes: the latitude of one might be ascending in the north and the other descending in the north, or both ascending in the south, or someone descending in the south. ### Distinction 13: The Frustrated Planets

<column-break/>

<margin>Alcabitius</margin>
And by a part of the dignity <note>original: "dignitatis"; refers to the essential strength a planet gains by being in certain signs or degrees.</note> in that same place, it sends its aspect to it, but its own [influence] and to those of the world; and this mode <term>Alcabitius</term> <note>original: "Alkobel"; Alcabitius was a 10th-century Arab astrologer whose work was a standard textbook in medieval Europe.</note> calls **reception**.

<margin>Returning Planet</margin>
**N**ote <note>original: "Memorandum"</note> that "returning" <note>original: "redduig" or "redduit"; an astrological condition where a planet returns its power to another.</note> is what occurs when a planet happens to join another planet that is **combust** <note>original: "combuiter"; a planet is 'combust' when it is so close to the Sun that its light and influence are hidden or 'burnt up'.</note> under the rays of the sun, or if it has lost its degree. Virtue is returned to it because of its weakness, by which its message does not reach that planet in an **angle** <note>original: "angulo"; the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses of a chart, where planets are most powerful.</note> or in the cadent houses or the middle houses with their own solar [qualities]. If that planet which is joined is in an angle, and the one it joins is also in an angle, or if there is no planet to join it, there will be a restoration <note>original: "redutio"</note> when it succeeds. This occurs whether it is a general restoration or a restoration to the **Lord** <note>original: "dominum"; the planet that rules a specific sign.</note> of the house.

<margin>Refrenated Planet</margin>
**W**hence follows <term>almuneza</term> <note>An Arabic-derived term for "refrenation."</note> or **refrenation**, and this happens when a planet seeks to join another, but before it can join, it begins a **retrogradation** <note>original: "retrogradatio"; when a planet appears to move backward in the sky from Earth's perspective.</note> and destroys what it intended. And secondly, this pertains to <margin>Interception</margin> **interception** or alteration and the "casting of light." This occurs when some light <note>fast-moving</note> planet is between two degrees, one in a sign and the other following <note>original: "podeos"; likely a corruption of the Greek 'proegoumenos' or 'hypodeomenos' regarding planetary order.</note>, such that they say the senior planet nearby wishes to join the following one; but before they join, that senior planet becomes retrograde while in the middle of those degrees, and subsequently it joins another, lighter planet. Then it is said that the heavy planet is bound to the following one.

<column-break/>

**L**ikewise, <term>Azarquiel</term> <note>original: "Alphazich"; refers to al-Zarqali, an 11th-century Andalusian astronomer.</note> describes **frustration**. This is when some **promissor** <note>original: "promissor"; the planet that 'promises' an event or outcome.</note> planet seeks to join another planet, but before it reaches it, that planet enters into another sign and joins with a different planet. This is called a "departure" <note>original: "appiacio"</note> from the sign; and the rays of the signs go out in this way because the planet of the first sign joins with another before the first [planet] reaches it or has anything to do with the others.

**Z**ahel <note>original: "Dancho"; likely a scribal corruption or specific reference to Sahl ibn Bishr, a 9th-century Jewish astrologer known in Latin as Zahel.</note> says that the **abscission of light** <note>original: "abscisio luminis"; a 'cutting off' of influence.</note> occurs when a planet seeks to join another with its light, and they are in the second sign from the sign of the one being joined. But before the joining occurs, the planet in the second sign becomes retrograde and joins another, which [cuts off] the light of the planet that wished to join it. That is, if a planet was bound to the love of another planet, and that other planet, while seeking to join, instead seeks to join a different "perfecting" planet. If, before the light planet reaches the degree, a **prohibition** <note>original: "prohibitio"; a condition where a third planet prevents two planets from forming an aspect.</note> joins it, it cuts off the light of that first lighter planet. <meta>catchword: to this planet</meta>

**T**here are also **intercepted places** in which planets suffer debility, and places in which they are fortunate, and places in which they are or were evil; then, through the places in which they are, as they were...

## Left Column

**Fortunes** <note>original: "fortune"; in astrology, these are the "benefic" planets, traditionally Jupiter and Venus, which are thought to bring good luck.</note> are those which are such by themselves or are in **good aspects** and other appearances of the good ones: namely, the **sextile** <note>original: "sextili"; an aspect where planets are 60 degrees apart, considered harmonious.</note> or the **trine** <note>original: "3o" or "trigona"; an aspect where planets are 120 degrees apart, the most favorable of all alignments.</note>. Also, there are those which are "burning" <note>original: "ardentes"; also known as **combust**, meaning a planet is too close to the Sun and its power is "burnt up" and hidden.</note> by them, which are partly absent and therefore are away from being a **fortune** in their rays.

<margin>Objection</margin>
This is the objection: whether it should please [the reader] to consider them fortunes or their rays. Another fortune brings its own rays through itself. They are also strengthened by being in **masculine** [signs] or increased in their modes.

<margin>Mars</margin>

### Distinction 4

<margin>Hyleg</margin>

### Calculation of the King's Part

The **Part of the King** is taken from the **Sun** in the beginning of the degree of **Leo** <note>original: "g[ra]dum leonis"</note> and projected from the **Moon** [unclear].

The hour of the election of the king is taken by the mediation of the world <term>Mediation of the world: Likely referring to the Aries Ingress or the 'Annus Mundi,' the moment the Sun enters Aries, used to predict the year's events for a kingdom.</term> in the middle of the night, when it is calculated and projected from the **ascendant** in the revolutions of the year by which the king is confirmed. 
If the beginning was in quartile signs <term>Quartile: Also known as a square aspect (90 degrees), traditionally considered a position of tension or challenge.</term>, and it was a diurnal revolution, then it ends the beginning by falling from the angles, etc.
The Part then is ascending in the night and it is added above 30 degrees from its own point from the **ascendant**; it begins and ends in the opposite, or both end falling from the **ascendant**.
This mediation existed for the purpose of balancing the world, if it should be between them as if from the **ascendant**.
And if the beginning ends in its **exaltation** <term>Exaltation: A specific sign where a planet is thought to have its most harmonious and powerful influence.</term> and the revolution was in the night, it should be taken from the table and projected from the **ascendant**.
There are two parts for conjunctions <note>The alignment of two celestial bodies</note>, then the time of the king's election and his longevity are similarly joined.

<meta>This page begins the foundational text of Western monasticism, the Rule of Saint Benedict. It introduces the four types of monks known in the early medieval period, categorizing them by their lifestyle and discipline.</meta>

### Here begins
## the kinds
# of monks

It is manifest that there are four kinds of monks. The first are the <term>Cenobites</term> <note>original: "coenobitarum"; monks who live in a community</note>, that is, those in a monastery serving under a rule or an abbot.

Then the second kind is the <term>Anchorites</term> <note>original: "anachoritarum"</note>, that is, hermits. These are people who have not been driven by a novice’s sudden burst of fervor, but have been tested by long endurance in a monastery. Having been taught by the support of many others, they have learned how to fight against the devil. Well-trained in the "brotherly line of battle," they move from the ranks of their brothers to the single combat of the desert. They are now secure enough to live without the consolation of another; with only their own hand or arm and with God’s help, they are able to fight against the vices of the flesh and their own thoughts.

The third and indeed most foul kind of monks is the <term>Sarabaites</term>. They have been approved by no rule nor tested by the experience of a master, as gold is tested in the furnace. Instead, they are as soft as lead. While they still keep faith with the world in their actions, they are known to lie to God by their <term>tonsure</term> <note>The practice of shaving the top of the head as a sign of religious devotion</note>. They live in twos or threes, or even alone, without a shepherd. They are not enclosed in the Lord's sheepfolds, but in their own. Their only law is the pleasure of their own desires; whatever they think of or choose, they call holy, and whatever they do not want, they consider forbidden.

The fourth kind of monks is called the <term>Gyrovagues</term> <note>Literally "circle-wanderers"</note>. Their whole life they wander through different regions, staying for three or four days in the cells of various people. They are always wandering and never stable, serving their own pleasures and the lures of gluttony. In every way, they are worse than the Sarabaites.

It is better to be silent than to speak of the most wretched lifestyle of all these people. Therefore, leaving all these aside, let us proceed, with the Lord's help, to organize the strongest kind: the Cenobites.

<summary>This page contains the first chapter of the Rule of Saint Benedict, defining the four types of monks: Cenobites, Anchorites, Sarabaites, and Gyrovagues. Benedict praises those who live under a rule while harshly criticizing wandering or undisciplined monks.</summary>

<keywords>monasticism, Rule of Saint Benedict, Cenobites, Anchorites, Sarabaites, Gyrovagues, hermits, monastic discipline</keywords>

# Here begins the book of Al-Kindi

I was asked previously, my dearest friend, because of the agreement of everyone concerning the celestial changes and their effects <note>original: "accidentiis"; in medieval science, an "accident" is a property or phenomenon rather than a mishap</note> in the clouds, winds, and moisture, according to probable reasons and causes. These matters have been distanced [from the truth] through the diverse judgments and the perversity of those judges whose knowledge was rightly rejected from their minds. They left the path of rectitude and believed that everything could be done by experience alone. They produced books and discourses and other things that were not likely to be true because of the imperfections of their own returns regarding the hour, and they manifest responses based only on the surface of things as they appear. Indeed, a man finds nothing unless he is shown how the truth can be demonstrated in the passions of the heavens; nor does he ascend to that knowledge except through natural steps and movements toward science. And by these means the sciences become clear. For just as when water rises, the celestial impressions are nourished by the heap [of vapors] above it. Therefore, because he does not find one who does not admit the truth, and they concur and know the same reason and follow the same will, we shall see and divide this book into eight chapters:

<margin>1</margin> The first is concerning all things fully and their causes and their influence in this <unclear>lower</unclear> world.
<margin>2</margin> The second is concerning the movements of the planets in their secondary motions.
<margin>3</margin> The third is concerning the quality of the year and the four [seasons] applying to them, regarding the <term>retrograde</term> <note>When a planet appears to move backward in the sky</note> and <term>direct</term> <note>When a planet moves in its normal forward direction</note> parts of its path.
<margin>4</margin> The fourth is concerning the winds and rains in every climate.
<margin>5</margin> The fifth is concerning the premeditated change and equality by which he calls both the year and the hour of its time.
<margin>6</margin> The sixth is concerning every place, using signs for things and rains through their gifts.
<margin>7</margin> The seventh is concerning the nature of the earth.

<column-break/>

<margin>8</margin> The eighth is concerning the times and <unclear>states</unclear> of the change of the air from hot to cold and vice-versa.

->The second book of Al-Kindi begins concerning changes, thunders, lightnings, winds, and rising vapors<-

The philosophers have agreed in this: that the nature of the world is one. They said that such planets are in their nature hot or cold, moist or dry, as is evident to the eye of the observers in their substance. They are hot, cold, moist, or dry, yet they do not sustain change in their bodies, nor diminution in themselves nor in any of their parts, except by their own motion under the circle of each in longitude and latitude, and also in their lowering, distancing, and heights. Each of these bodies is seen as larger in appearance according to its distance from us; and at another time they are distanced from one appearance to another where they seem larger. They also said that a planet is not made of fire, nor is its light from fire. They said the sun is the hottest of the planets, and the solar roots are formed strongly in the earth—a little more than two—because the sun and the earth are of equal quantity <note>The author is discussing the proportional influence of the sun's heat relative to its size and distance</note>. It is said that its nature exists such that if it were not distant, every time would be the same. For I say certainly that these planets are weakened and rendered "unfortunate" in their distance from one another and from the equinox; and there would be a greater impulse of heat if the days remained equal, and the time would be of one nature, either hot or cold. As is taken from the books of the sun in the chapters on Capricorn and Gemini, that part is measured equally and flows through the east from the sign of Gemini, and it is at its highest point unless it is at the furthest point of Capricorn. <margin>double and strong</margin>
Its intensity approaches, but from the southern part, and then the winds are unleashed <note>original: "immitentes"; the OCR is unclear, but the context suggests the release or movement of winds</note>, just as when the sun begins its apogee <term>aux: the point in a planet's orbit furthest from the Earth; medieval astronomers believed the sun's distance changed the intensity of its heat</term>. ## On the Aspects of the Gates . e .

Matters are differentiated according to some concerning the aspects signified in time toward one another, just as proximity [or] another is said by way of a hammer <note>original: "malleam"; possibly referring to a striking or forceful aspect</note>, etc. For the mistress <note>original: "domina"; typically referring to the Moon in this context</note> in her comparisons [states] that the lord of the aspect of the gates—which is the foundation—is the inferior planet <note>term: "inferior planet"; planets closer to the Sun than Earth (Mercury and Venus), thought to move more quickly and influence the lower atmosphere</note> when it is in a superior one <note>term: "superior planet"; planets further from the Sun (Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn)</note>, and then these are opposite the body of the house of a benevolent [planet]. When it was generated with the Moon, or with an aspect, there is an opening of the gates <note>term: "apertio portarum"; an astrological event believed to 'open' the heavens to release rain, wind, or storms</note>, just as when the Sun is generated... the house with the Sun, just as they are opposite their own houses. As by the properties of the opening, many are found among them that have houses through the opposition of both... whatever is generated to be sent after the opening of the work, the body through opposition, because the lowest note <note>original: "hypatessum"; a term borrowed from Greek musical theory, here likely describing the lowest orbital position</note> was retrograde in humidity in autumn, [bringing] winds, but it is neglected. It signifies the sea where then toward the epidemic <note>original: "epidemiam"; historically used to describe a general corruption of the air or a widespread disease</note> in the south and heat... to see winds from the left in a true birth... just as the Moon separated from acting on some planet, or sometimes the "bringing near" between another planet according to the dogma of those opposite planets. This is the black rays of Capricorn [and] Balhaz the Great <note>original: "balhaz"; likely referring to the astronomer Abu Ma'shar, known as Albumasar in the West</note> which is in the sea. Winds and rain [are] not then, for he asked of those planets with the Moon separating, to prepare the generation to be sent from the separation of both... separating from the Sun they make the generation; this is the opening of the four valves <note>original: "valvarum"; often used interchangeably with 'gates' to describe atmospheric apertures</note>.

# Book of Weather Forecasts

<margin>

birth, place, Saturn, Jupiter, Mars

The diagnosis of the disposition of various arts concerning future events, as it begins from the motion of the higher powers <note>original: "supiorū potestatū"; referring to the celestial bodies</note>, is within our ability through all natural actions, the qualities of the quarters of the circle, the writing of revolutions, and the showing of the divine. There are 12 signs, and they are distinguished by their elemental natures. First: **Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius** are of a fiery nature, hot and dry. **Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn** are of an earthly nature, cold and dry. **Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius** are of an airy nature, hot and moist. **Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces** are of a watery nature, cold and moist. 

The natures of the planets are most perfect: **Saturn** is extremely cold and somewhat dry, and because of this, it is by its own nature the enemy of all things. **Jupiter** is temperately hot and moist, and is a friend to all nature. **Mars**, however, is temperately hot and moist <note>The text here contains a common scribal variation; Mars is usually described as excessively hot and dry, but this manuscript notes its "superfluous heat"</note> or excessively hot, and is contrary to all natural things; just as it moves with a Great Force, it abounds in heat and sharpness. The **Sun** is temperately hot, and because of this, it claims all the qualities of natural life. **Venus** is very temperately hot on the surface and moist, whence she is said to have dominion over all venereal <note>term: "venereal"; in this historical context, it refers to things governed by Venus, such as beauty, growth, and desire</note> things. **Mercury** administers through its own nature according to the planet or sign it is joined with, being said to be of whatever nature it is attached to. The **Moon**, by its own nature, is temperately cold and moist, though it is said to follow the Sun's heat, even if it remains temperately cold. 

But it is also said that there are certain strengths in the signs which are attributed to the planets, which are called "dignities" <note>term: "dignities"; the various ways a planet gains strength or influence based on its position in the zodiac</note> or affinities. These are: 
1. **House** <note>original: "domus"</note>
2. **Exaltation** <note>original: "exaltatio"</note>
3. **Triplicity** <note>original: "triplicitas"</note>
4. **Term** <note>original: "termini"</note>
5. **Face** <note>original: "ffacies"</note>

Sun
