Fortune of the days of the planets
</margin>

<column-break/>

<margin>
Essential houses of the planets
</margin>
Each planet has its own house where its strength is manifest. A planet in its own **house** is like a lord in his own domain or lordship. In its **exaltation**, it is in its glory and fullness of power, like one in his honor. A planet in its **triplicity** is powerful like one among his kinsmen and people. A planet in its **term** is powerful like one in his own office or magistry. A planet in its **face** is like one with his master. The **aspects**, however, are powerful according to the strength and validity of their proximity, for an aspect that is "bad" acts like a correction of the stars.

<margin>
Accidental houses of the planets
</margin>
The houses of the planets are those parts in which the origin of the world was established <note>term: "origin of the world"; a reference to the *Thema Mundi*, a mythical horoscope showing the positions of the planets at the moment of creation</note>. Thus, **Leo** is the house of the Sun; **Cancer** of the Moon; **Virgo** of Mercury; **Libra** of Venus; **Aries** of Mars; **Sagittarius** of Jupiter; and **Capricorn** of Saturn. It is said that the planets have their primary dwellings as follows: Saturn in [Aquarius], Jupiter in [Pisces], Mars in Scorpio, Venus in Taurus, and Mercury in Gemini. From this, their friendship and domicile are declared.

<margin>
Exaltations of the planets
</margin>
The **exaltations** of the planets are as follows: the Sun is exalted in Aries; the Moon in Taurus; Saturn in Libra; Mars in Capricorn; Jupiter in Cancer; Venus in Pisces; and Mercury in Virgo. When a planet is in the sign opposite its exaltation, it is in its "fall" or "depression" <note>original: "detrimento"</note>, as the Sun in Libra is in its descent from its highest point.

<margin>
Triplicities of the planets
</margin>
The **triplicities** of the planets are groups of signs of the same nature. For example, the Sun's triplicity is in Sagittarius and Aries, which are fiery, hot, and dry, just like Leo, in which the Sun was established at the beginning.

<margin>
Terms of the planets
</margin>
Regarding the **terms**, various authors say different things, but according to the Egyptians, they are these: Jupiter has the first six degrees of Aries; Venus the next six; Mercury the next eight; Mars the next five; and Saturn the last ones, as appears in the written signs below.

<margin>
Faces of the planets
</margin>
The **faces** <note>term: "face"; also known as a decan, a division of a zodiac sign into three equal parts of 10 degrees each</note> are those by which the signs are distinguished into three equal parts. For example, in Aries, which has two faces <note>The text likely means "three faces," a common scribal slip or specific variant</note>: the first face is from the beginning to the 10th degree of Aries and is said to be of Mars; the second face is up to the 20th degree and is said to be the face of the Sun, who...

<meta>This page continues the technical explanation of planetary influences, moving from the "essential dignities" (inherent strengths) to "accidental dignities"—strengths gained through relationships with other planets (aspects) and their specific orbital motions (retrogradation, station, etc.).</meta>

<margin>
Aspects
Opposition
Affliction
</margin>
There are also other fortunes and weaknesses which the planets receive from one another through their **aspects** <note>term: "aspects"; the geometric angles between planets as seen from Earth, which astrologers believe determine how planets interact</note>. A planet receives either a good fortune or a "bad weakness" from another through a [harmful] aspect. There are several aspects: the **opposition**, the **quartile**, the **sextile**, the **trine**, and the fifth aspect <note>original: "quiert⁹"; likely referring to the conjunction, which is often listed with the four major aspects</note>. An opposition occurs when planets are in [opposing] signs; this aspect is called the **worst** and most difficult, especially if the qualities of the planets are contrary to one another. For example, if Venus <note>associated with moisture and heat</note> is in Aries and Saturn <note>associated with cold and dryness</note> is in Libra, the planets strike each other with contrary natures. This is why an opposition is the most harmful.
<margin>
Trine
The Best
</margin>
The third aspect occurs when two planets are in signs that hold a **trine** <note>term: "trine"; a 120-degree angle, considered the most harmonious relationship</note> between them. This is called the "best aspect" because there are no contrary qualities in the relationship. If planets like Jupiter and Venus are there, they grant great [benefits].
<margin>
Quartile
Mediocre
Bad
</margin>
A **quartile** <note>term: "quartile"; also called a "square," a 90-degree angle</note> occurs when the aspect between two planets is not a full three signs apart—for example, if a planet is in Aries and Saturn is in Cancer. It is called a quartile because the planet occupies a fourth part of the zodiac. This aspect is called **mediocre bad**, acting like a hidden deceiver.
<margin>
Sextile
Mediocre
Good
</margin>
The **sextile** <note>term: "sextile"; a 60-degree angle</note> occurs when there are two signs between the planets. This is called **mediocre good**.
<margin>
Conjunction
Strongest
</margin>
A **conjunction** <note>original: "iuctio"; when two planets appear in the same spot in the sky</note> is the strongest of the aspects. It occurs when planets are in the same sign, such as Aries. This is considered the most powerful interaction, as it creates a shared temperament between them. There are also other fortunes and weaknesses which planets receive from being in their "small circle," which is called the **epicycle** <note>term: "epicycle"; in pre-Copernican astronomy, a small circle that a planet follows, the center of which moves along a larger circle (the deferent)</note>.

<column-break/>

These [accidental conditions] are rising and setting, progression, station, and retrogradation. The **rising** <note>term: "rising"; specifically heliacal rising, when a planet becomes visible in the dawn sky after being hidden by the Sun's glare</note> of a planet is said to occur when it emerges from under the solar rays and clearly appears, no longer hindered by the Sun's brightness. **Progression** occurs when a planet moves sensibly forward in its path. **Retrogradation** <note>term: "retrogradation"; the illusion that a planet is moving backward in the sky due to the Earth's relative motion</note> is when it [appears to move] from east to west. **Station** is when it seems to stand still while changing direction. 

There is also another distinction among the planets according to their work in their **deferent** <note>term: "deferent"; the large circular orbit that carries the planet's epicycle around the Earth</note>, which is admirable and worthy of study. Planets are found to be weaker in the lower part of their deferents and stronger in the higher part. Two different effects are observed based on these locations. When planets are at their **apogee** <note>term: "apogee"; the point in an orbit farthest from the Earth</note>, they have a different operation than when they are at the opposite of the apogee [perigee]. This is due to the speed of motion and the heat preserved by the planet's distance from the equator. The planet describes circles... one half of the zodiac is descending and the other is ascending. The ascending part, for us, is from the point of **Capricorn** through to the end of **Gemini**. A planet is said to be descending when it moves from the point of **Cancer** through to the end of **Sagittarius**, retreating from us toward the south. These circles exist not because the planet itself moves the deferent, but because the circles in which it is carried are distant from the equator... as is seen in the rising of the orbits.

# Here begins the prologue to the Compendium on the Impressions and Changes of the Air

Because the wise men of old produced and left behind many writings concerning the transformations and changes of the air <note>original: "mutationibus aeris"; in this period, meteorology was understood as the study of changes in the atmosphere caused by celestial influence</note> treating this subject—just as in other matters where things are lost by being set aside—those specific treatises are obscure and presented metaphorically. Others, however, do not treat the works of the ancients at all, and some rarely cite them openly, which leads some to feel envy. Therefore, I have sought to compose so many books into a single treatise to clarify obscure matters through the understanding of the senses. I aim to reconcile those authors where they disagree or to separate the points they make from others, because the sayings of the ancients remain scattered among them and are often corrupted. For this reason, I have undertaken to organize these works for the benefit of the faithful and to bring others that serve the same purpose into one single body <note>original: "unum corpus"; a "corpus" is a collection of related writings</note>. Though they may seem to disagree, they can be reconciled. I intend to cite their books faithfully throughout the treatise so that if anyone doubts a point, they can refer back to those books and perhaps add more from a reporter's account without changing the original intent. It can also be easily seen that this work is of great value, as we may more easily find and compare many books and many teachers in their own sections. By comparing them, they will be seen to agree more closely through certain things that are proven by opinion, but which are to be approved through experience—which is composed of the senses, time, and long duration—in which I have seen.

<column-break/>

Those who involve themselves in this art are not deceived in their worldly affairs; for many books of teachings benefit us greatly during difficult times and regarding stellar matters. Indeed, some are arranged by chapters according to precise times, as much by the months as by the Sun, which can return what is owed to God concerning the days in which He named them <note>The author is likely referring to the religious significance of the calendar and the "days of creation" as they relate to natural cycles</note>, which would be to rely on space and

<margin>221 2</margin> 
The second part concerns the variety introduced into the changes of the air through the four seasons, the rules <note>original: "reguas," likely "regulas"</note>, eclipses, the solar points of the year in their various parts and in any other locations, and concerning the years, months, and the four signs <note>This refers to the "cardinal signs" of the zodiac: Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn, which mark the changes of the seasons</note>.

<margin>231 3</margin> 
The third part concerns universal changes in every climate 
<margin>231</margin> through the four and opposite signs. <note>Refers to the astrological aspects of squares and oppositions</note>

### The Effects of Planetary Motion on Heat and Cold

The cold effects are sometimes finished <note>original: "finit aliqn"</note> more strongly in the middle part. Likewise, the heat of a planet is stronger in other parts. There is another doubt in the first treatise regarding whether the effect is stronger when the planet is outside [the rays] or when it is under them.

Likewise, all the **heavy planets** <note>original: "pite ponderosi"; referring to the superior planets: Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn.</note> from their appearance until they reach **opposition** <term>opposition: the position of a planet when it is exactly opposite the Sun in the sky</term>, and from opposition until they descend to their setting, [change their qualities]. Likewise, in the same reasoning, until their conjunction <note>original: "glustioz", likely a scribal error for "coniunctionem"</note> they are cooling, and from conjunction until the **first station** they are warming, for the strength is more valid in **retrogradation** <term>retrogradation: the period where a planet appears to move backward through the zodiac</term>.

Likewise, the strength of the stations and the declination <note>original: "declaratoe ronal"</note> in the south are more cooling, whereas the appearance and inclination in the south are more heating... without brief [interruption] this effect occurs.

Likewise, **Venus**, when she emerges and sets or is retrograde, has a liquid quality. When she is oriental [rising before the Sun], she is heating; when she is oriental and enduring, she descends; when she is oriental and [in another phase], she cools. Her quality in the first part from the Sun is hot and moist... and she is suitable for the autumn and the harvest. When she is in her station, she is moist. In the first part, her path is equal and hot. In the middle, she is cold, and in her station she is now cooling; while descending she diminishes, for in her fourth and fifth parts from the Sun, she is moist and independent.

Likewise, it is noted that **retrograde planets** signify rain, especially the **inferior planets** <note>original: "inferiores"; Mercury and Venus, whose orbits are between the Earth and the Sun.</note> which are under the Sun; and commonly, whether they are inferior or nearby, if they are in **feminine signs** <term>feminine signs: Earth and Water signs (Taurus, Cancer, Virgo, Scorpio, Capricorn, Pisces), traditionally considered cold and moist</term>, they are more cloudy. They are clearer in other signs and colder... this is according to **Abraham** <note>referring to Abraham Ibn Ezra, a 12th-century scholar and astrologer.</note> and **Ptolemy** regarding why a planet is retrograde.

<column-break/>

In the first descent toward the opposition of the Sun, there was no rain, but from the opposition to the [second] station, there is rain...

Likewise, **Saturn**, when he is under the [Sun's] rays in the morning, causes rains and coldness or cloudiness. In the evening, he is the ruler of heat and heavy [storms], ripening the seeds; his temperament is good. He produces thunder and lightning in the first part of the morning. Under the rays, he makes rains; in the evening, clouds and [storms]... in the morning, he provides a serene sky. He makes thunder and lightning in the middle of the [season]. Under the rays, he is cold; in the evening, heavy; when mature, he brings a troubled time of **winter storms** <note>original: "Bronail", likely for "brumali", referring to the winter solstice or winter weather.</note> with lightning and thunder. In the autumn, under the rays in the morning or evening, he causes rain or a serene autumn. Under the rays, he is impetuous in the evening... his morning temperament is clear.

**Jupiter**, under the rays in the summer <note>original: "ethauno", likely for "aestivo"</note>, is good for the grain. In the evening, he is steady; he is good for the grain and brings lightning and thunder. Under the cloudy and impetuous [skies], **Jupiter** in the summer under the rays is moderate. In the evening, he signifies showers; in the morning, he is moist... in the winter <note>original: "Bronail"</note> he is steady. In the morning, under the rays, he signifies the ripening of the grain. **Jupiter** in **Taurus** <note>original: "tautos"</note> under the rays signifies thunder; in the evening, the ripening of the grain is good and rare. In Taurus, under the rays, he brings thunder, is stormy and shadowy; in the evening, the grain is well-ripened, dewy, and moist.

Likewise, in **Gemini**, under the rays in the evening, he is arid; in the morning, he brings thunder. This temperament brings lightning and thunder; thus, **Jupiter** in Gemini under the rays signifies [complex] grain and steady winter storms.

It is emitted through **Mars**, and by his approach and retreat his heat increases; he dries [the air] with heat and dryness, as discussed previously. These [effects] occur in one year and in a natural cycle which is at one time humid and at another time dry. But whenever a planet in its course separates itself to withdraw from its signs, then it is stronger than the humid forces and hotter, and it nurtures its fruits. I call [the influence] descending humidity, and its heat nourishes; and when it is a sign of rain, it causes sparks, thunders, rays, and performs wonders in the air. It is weakened in watery signs and strong in fiery signs. Therefore, it is said by the wise and expert that soon a part [of the influence] in the waters—as in the pressures of winter—is tied to humidity and rain. ¶ If it is **retrograde** <term>retrograde: the apparent backward motion of a planet in the sky</term> while the Sun remains, then rain and humidity will be rare; then in that matter, it is understood through its approach to the Sun and its movement **under the Sun's rays** <note>original: "sub radios solis"; meaning the planet is too close to the Sun to be visible.</note>. ¶ And there will be [other] signs of rain through the air and through the world, according to its movement from sign to sign and through its stations, whether it returns to its course or to its two points of opposition. When it travels its paths in direct motion and in the strength of its body, at that time it is said to hold the signs; and when it is fortunate or retrograde, they signify strong, direct humidities and rains, and movements in the mists and in the clouds and similar things. Just as the Moon, when placed in other watery signs, [signifies] through these distinctions. ¶ Also, according to **John of Seville** <note>Johannes Hispalensis: a prominent 12th-century translator of Arabic scientific texts into Latin.</note>, a planet wishing [to exert] its part in rain has power, and it rains according to the quality of that sign. For in the same place as the eye <note>original: "aculi," likely a reference to the 'eye' of a constellation like Taurus.</note>, rain is signified by the aforementioned certainty according to the nature of the planets, which in their purity give fit spaces to the earth.

<column-break/>

For in [human] bodies and then in part through changes, it is so consumed by fire or by dryness that it leads [to heat], and every part is affected by the ascent of the prior heat to the highest point. In this, when it emerges from any of the **angles** <term>angles: the four most powerful houses in an astrological chart (1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th)</term>, the air becomes certain... in the hand and in the manner of the sick by direct motion. Let it be done just as the parts appear in nature; so also the appearance of the stars signifies their own [effects]. Also according to **Abu Ma'shar** <note>Albumasar: a famous 9th-century Persian astrologer whose works were fundamental to European astrology.</note>, regarding the leadership [of the planets], if they precede the rains before the Sun and Moon, it is not so; and some other part is hotter, and likewise concerning the winter in its own way. Also according to Abu Ma'shar, regarding the cleanliness [of the air], good rain is had from the approach and retreat of the sea <note>original: "accessibz et recessibz maris"; referring to the tides.</note> according to the motion of the light [the Moon]. Also, the power of the planets is discussed. Also, Abu Ma'shar in the **sixth distinction** <note>A reference to a specific chapter in his 'Greater Introduction to Astrology'.</note>, which treats the middle [planets?], brings this to the proposition when he speaks of the influence found there. ¶ Yet, according to how they are seized, because they enter at night under the rays, not all quadrants can be placed; if it is placed, perhaps a man is compelled to place... ¶ Also, the power of the planets is increased when they are distant from the Sun, and likewise when they are distant from the **houses of the Moon** <note>The 'mansions' or 'domiciles' of the Moon.</note>, then they rule **face to face** <note>original: "facie ad facie"; referring to an aspect of opposition (180 degrees).</note>. Also, the strength of the planets [is increased] if they are in their own houses. Also, those that are in the angles or in the **succedents** <term>succedent: the houses following the angles (2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th), considered to have moderate strength</term> are more powerful than those that fall in the middle. ¶ Also, planets are **exalted** <note>Exaltation is a state where a planet's influence is particularly harmonious and strong.</note> above others when one is higher than another, so that the planet is at its highest point above the earth. Also, in whatever sign a planet gives to another, etc., which is given according to the habit of the sign and its planet.

<meta>This page transitions from the catalog of fixed stars into a treatise on the nature of the planets and the four seasons, specifically focusing on the influence of Saturn (Zuhaul) and the astrological effects of retrograde motion on weather and the environment. It continues the astronomical theme but shifts toward "computus" (calculation) and natural philosophy.</meta>

The stars of <term>Zuhaul</term> <note>The Arabic name for the planet Saturn</note> are not visible in these regions; they are of the first magnitude. Because the latitude of their bodies is so great, it appears to you that they do not show themselves above the horizon in their own places. Therefore, also for me, <term>Alphonso</term> <note>Referring to King Alfonso X of Castile, sponsor of the Alfonsine Tables</note>, from the tradition of those tables given to John of Sicily, I have completed the calculation of the motion of the fixed stars in the predicted time, combining three into one, which gives the equal motion of the body of the same name for a year: 38 seconds, 2 thirds, 49 fourths, 3 fifths, 24 sixths. <note>These are technical sexagesimal fractions used in medieval astronomy to define the slow movement of the stars, known as precession.</note>

<margin>Extracted from <term>Albumasar</term> <note>Abu Ma'shar, a highly influential 9th-century Persian astrologer</note> in the 4th distinction, 2nd chapter, and it agrees with this.</margin>
**T**here are four seasons of the year: **Spring** <note>original: "Ver"</note> beginning from <term>Aries</term> is hot and moist; **Summer** <note>original: "Estas"</note> in <term>Cancer</term> is hot and dry; **Autumn** <note>original: "Autumpnus"</note> from <term>Libra</term> is cold and dry; and **Winter** <note>original: "Hyems"</note> from <term>Capricorn</term> is cold and moist. And the order of the seasons is most fit for the proportion of the movement and so forth, even when a planet is <term>retrograde</term> <note>Appearing to move backward in the sky from the perspective of Earth</note>.

**F**or everyone knows that in the winter time, it is dry; but truly, through the melting of ice, it is made moist. It is mostly fulfilled through the three retrograde stages, and if there is a dire debility <note>An astrological state where a planet is "weak" due to its position</note> there, it takes the form of moisture. When a planet is retrograde in the autumn, it takes the form of moisture for that time. When it is retrograde in the winter, it takes the form of dryness. When it is retrograde in the summer, having come from a spring sign, there is the highest heat in that part of the time, from which the air is cooled and hot winds are stirred up; and because it will have power over the plants, there will still be heat outside, but in the depths of the earth, it will be colder. But if there were two leaders <note>referring to planetary aspects or "rectors"</note> before the summer is finished, the heat is weakened, and the harmful cold is mitigated through its endurance when the Sun is in an angle, etc. But if it were then in the west, that part would be weaker because after the setting of the Sun, it approaches the zenith of the head <note>original: "amity capitu"</note>. In summer, if it is retrograde in autumn, it takes the form of heat in that time.

<column-break/>

They will dry out. Southern winds will enter. If it stays in summer... and is dry, it is a figure of heat and dryness. Then, if it is retrograde in autumn in a spring sign, then the Sun works... in that part, the time coordinating the complexion <note>The "complexion" refers to the balance of the four qualities: hot, cold, moist, and dry</note>. The nights would be cold, and if the debility of heat is dire, there will be extreme frost. In autumn, if it is retrograde in an autumnal sign, the heat of the sun is moved in that part, or the moisture will be multiplied there, and the things that were frozen there will be dissolved. But if it is dry, there will be extreme frost in that part, or when there are winds from the south, which signifies a change in the winter sign. When it is retrograde in a spring sign, it is a figure of moisture because then the sun dissolves the air, or the winds are multiplied; but when there is a dire debility, it takes the form of moisture at that time, especially if it is visible from the sun. Then, if it is retrograde in autumn, there will be the highest moisture in that time, or there will be many winds, and with this, the sun dissolves the frost. But if it is not dire, there will be black clouds and moisture in that time. In winter, if it is retrograde in a winter sign, it is a figure of moisture; but if it is then dire, it is a figure of dryness. Through this, it is shown that in such a time of year, one should take the "head" <note>the beginning of a zodiac sign</note> from the head of Aries, and if it is retrograde, there will be few but beautiful days; or it will be moist until the end. If it is dry and moist <gloss>dry</gloss>, there will be strong floods or deluges in the spring or in the autumn. But if no planet is retrograde, it will not be so.

<meta>This page continues the discussion on planetary influences, shifting from the specific motions of Saturn to the broader effects of planetary retrogradation and the division of the earth and time. ...being vacant for its other seven [planets], according to their present nature, there will be **dryness**, even if some body [planet] is moved in **retrograde** <note>The apparent backward motion of a planet in the sky.</note> from its own nature. Which, in the course of time, through its significations, is said to cause a difference in the return of those things which all planets do in their **retrogradation**. From two or three [planets], it is said that in the winter season there occurs a strong coldness; if it were a neutral planet, it would be strong in its nature, as the body which returns in the fourth [house] <note>The astrological "house" associated with the home and the end of life.</note> of the year would be various. And it is said that in winter, the signs are in agreement with themselves in these matters elsewhere.

**Also**, whether some light or mixed elements are assumed from the cold signs or frost, it leads to a state in the winter season of clouds and southern winds. However, in the spring season, it leads to clouds or a moderate temperament, while in the summer, it leads to lightning and thunder. These things are described as having weaker effects above than those mentioned elsewhere.

**Also**, the day is divided from the rising of the sun to midday; then the sun moves from midday until sunset; then it remains from sunset until midnight; and from midnight to the rising of the sun. This is stated elsewhere in the science of <term>Computus</term> <note>The medieval science of calculating time and the dates of religious feasts.</note>.

**Also**, in [chapters] 21 and 22, the associates of <term>Abu Ma'shar</term> <note>original: "Albnasar"; 9th-century Persian astrologer Abu Ma'shar al-Balkhi.</note> have written concerning the natures of the times of the year, and in chapter 41, they speak of the ruler of time. Note that the superior planets <note>The planets further from the sun than Earth: Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn.</note> are not said to be retrograde from the sun in the same way. **Leopold** <note>Leopold of Austria, a 13th-century astronomer.</note> says that for the superior planets, this can only occur through an aspect or proceeding. According to **Abu Ma'shar**, 16 days are reckoned outside the number of hours in the effectiveness of the world, which are throughout the parts of the year and the 12 houses <note>The twelve divisions of the astrological chart.</note>, if it were through the signs.

<column-break/>

Those which from an <term>aspect</term> <note>The angular distance between two planets, believed to create a specific influence.</note> are opposite signs are said to be discordant and masculine; others are feminine. There are four angles, four dense regions, and four falling [cadent] houses, following the four lunar phases according to their nature and proximity.

**Now**, the times are not the same in every way in every land. The angles are diminished according to their approach; they do not approach from the <term>equator</term> <note>original: "equoctiali"</note> through the fixed boundaries. The middle region is temperate, the southern is hot, and the northern is cold. Concerning this, see elsewhere in the work on the year by **Ptolemy** <note>original: "ptholmeu"; the 2nd-century Alexandrian polymath.</note>, in the first chapter of the twelfth book. And there, compare the qualities of the winds according to their own parts, which **Ptolemy** concorded according to his own boundaries or according to the four parts.

**Also**, the years in which there are rains are found in the 1st, 9th, 5th, and 6th [cycles], while in others there is nothing but dryness, depending on the heat and cold, or the severity of the frost and the changes mentioned in the fifth chapter.

**Also**, therefore, from what has been said briefly regarding the angle of the habitable world between the four <term>triplicities</term> <note>Groups of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, Water).</note>. The first and fourth govern and move throughout the entire three-fold world. They correspond to the angle which is the South, and the succeeding signs govern through the aspects they make. The second and third signs govern the angle of the earth through their conjunction and aspect. The signs corresponding to the angle which is South and West govern the world thereafter, as mentioned in chapter 12 and the 1st and 4th parts of the 2nd book.

**Also**, which locations and which cities belong to each sign, and which quantity corresponds to another figure through the boundaries and degrees of men, as found in the 2nd part of the 1st book of **Ptolemy**, and outside of this declaration in the eighth book concerning these matters.

It should be known that in a **great conjunction** <note>A significant alignment of the outer planets—Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars—historically believed to cause major shifts in weather and world events.</note> of the three superior [planets], a change in the conditions of the entire upper air is signified. If they appear in **fiery signs** <note>Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius.</note>, they cause heat in the air. If in their descents <note>Positions in the zodiac where a planet's influence is considered weakened.</note>, they cause dryness and tremors. In **watery signs** <note>Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces.</note>, however, they cause an intemperance in the air and a multitude of winds with a moderate amount of cold. In **dry signs**, understand the same.
And understand this same thing regarding the **conjunction of Saturn and Mars**. And this is found in the conjunctions of <term>Masha'allah</term> <note>original: "messahalah"; an 8th-century Persian Jewish astrologer and astronomer who was a leading authority on conjunctions.</note> in chapters 9, 10, and 11.

When Saturn is in permanent signs <note>Also known as "fixed" signs: Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius.</note> during a conjunction, or is aspecting them, or directs its rays toward them, it corrupts the air by its aspect. If it is hindered in **earthy signs**, it causes darkness of the air and tremors. If in **dry signs**, it is joined to cold and the blowing of unstable winds. If in **water**, it causes submersions and floods. And according to the measure of its strength in that place, the effect will be as it is found in the *Flowers of Abu Ma'shar*, 7th treatise.

Likewise, the conjunction of Saturn and Mars in Aries—which corresponds to sleep and <unclear>hier-</unclear>—is because of dryness and other signifiable air. Likewise, when the body of Jupiter was in the lunar <unclear>testro</unclear> because of its conjunctions on the horizons. Likewise, when the body is in the upper Leo because of the aspect of the sun in dry signs. Likewise, when the body of Mars is in Scorpio, then there occurs a noted change of waters and a mutability of clouds.

<meta>This page continues the medieval astrological discourse from the previous folio. Before the eclipse <unclear>there were</unclear> applications and separations <note>original: "applicationes et separationes"; these are astrological terms describing planets moving toward or away from an aspect or connection with each other</note> in this or that manner according to the properties of the sign, or those [planets] which were in the house of their exaltations, triplicities, or in the horoscope <note>the "horoscope" here refers to the Ascendant, the sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the eclipse</note>. It signifies for humanity endless rains; and if the lord of the place of the <term>eclipse</term> <note>original: "clipis"; likely a scribal variant or contraction of "eclipsis"</note> shall be there, it does not [signify rain], but if it has many dignities there, it adds what was of autumn in its own time. Afterwards, these are to be understood through the figures and constitutions which are to be considered through those things in the sign of the eclipse, or in the angles <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses of a chart, which are considered the most powerful locations for planets</note> that are before or after the eclipse. And that which at the time of the eclipse is in such an aspect or union, for that reason it rules according to the time and place of the eclipse. They are figured by the <note>original: "bethenae"; possibly referring to an Arabic astrological term or a corruption of a technical name</note> opening of lightning in which it was strong through the term of the eclipses. It signifies the opening of an earthquake, the ruin of castles, and death by air without end. <meta>This page marks the beginning of the *Centiloquium*, a famous collection of 100 astrological aphorisms. It follows the introductory matter or a previous volume. The text establishes the foundational philosophy of astrology as a cooperation between the heavens and the human mind.</meta>

# Here begins the Hundred Sayings of Ptolemy

The change of worldly things toward this state or that occurs through the movement of the celestial bodies, which are the renewers of those things; contemplate the first celestial movements. <note>The *Centiloquium* (or *Kapnos*) is a collection of 100 aphorisms once attributed to the 2nd-century astronomer Claudius Ptolemy, though now considered to be by a later author, likely of Arabic origin.</note> // For the goodness of souls <note>original: "animae"</note> comes from you and from them <note>The phrase "A te et ab illis" (From you and from them) is the core of this first aphorism, suggesting that astrological judgment depends on both the stars and the intuition of the astrologer.</note>. It must be said that the judgment of those previous things is according to the form of particular effects, just as it is not necessary to assign a cause for the individual forms of trials. // And more so, it is not fitting for him who is to be the master of his own judgments and their quality, because one should not signify based on a form that is acting in truth; for the judgment of this form and its universality are complementary and received. Therefore, my friend <note>original: "ur amei", likely "amice"</note>, consider the first indications in their own nature and in a similar way between truth and existence; this is because I am led toward all things and all opposites. // <term>Haly</term> <note>Haly refers to Ali ibn Ridwan, a famous 11th-century Egyptian physician and astrologer whose commentary on Ptolemy was standard in medieval universities.</note>. The science of the stars is from you and from them, for one must not decree specific effects like someone who sees something and simply reacts. // For thus does he act who considers his own proper thing, which he keeps until the knowledge of it comes to him; it is from the coming of these things that one acts on doubts through the reported form, and these indications, just as they are, are between nature and property. // <term>Ptolemy</term> said that these indications are of a natural nature; this is possible according to him because he considers the nature of things and the work of the stars. // Well for those who have a better part of the knowledge of things to come; they were more proper in their knowledge because of the entire indication, although not many have this possession. // Ptolemy said "from you and from them," which signifies that he who desires to foreknow future things must use two ways: one is the movement of the stars, and the other is the work that exists in things according to the movement of the causes and the members which he reflects upon among the proportions of their own movements; and to the changes of the highest ones, which he proved in his own time.

<margin>
Of <unclear>canis</unclear> and <unclear>visigo</unclear> <note>These may be corrupted names of stars or constellations, possibly Sirius (Canis) and another.</note> who is from <unclear>manti</unclear> is <unclear>to be noted</unclear>.
</margin>

<column-break/>

"From them": The other way is that which someone has through divine inspirations; those who consider things through this way can give many true indications, for which they do not need the figure or the voice of the thing; for the worker without work or without inspiration acts through the divine, or it flows into their hearts, and from many many people it is seen that this way was with the philosophers when they were under divine influence. // Therefore, it is said that those who are under the moon, since they had in them a certain knowledge through the teaching of another, or through the power of the gods, or by Imanu-el; one or the other who did not have these two ways are less wise and will tremble when they provide their own judgments. // If an indicator lacks any star, he will never be truly wise; this is what Ptolemy said, for he who speaks of the future ought not to speak of a specific power as though it were destined, but rather the strength of the trials and of the wise, which regards the whole work of the stars in their nobility toward one thing and another. Therefore, he says not "specific power" in the way of the effects of heat, but he maintains the effects of other things by the efficacy of heat in the manner of divine wills. // It is said that a person is guided from a chosen part toward a common change, which only the power of the soul, which knows in hope, recognizes what joy it gives and what light. // For this power is strong over greed and because it has made us separate from the world, it takes away from us the knowledge of the future.

<margin>
<image-desc>A manicule (pointing hand) points toward the line beginning with "because it has made us".</image-desc>
If you wish the effect to be removed from the mind, [then] the knowledge of the future [is also removed].
</margin>

But if this power is always healthy, we might be better able to foreknow future things, just as we see many hermits who predicted future things; and some of the Peripatetics <note>Followers of Aristotle's school of philosophy.</note> who, when they are in consideration of these things, then their bodies are not hindered by what they see, but by the sole power of the soul, they see future or present things in the form in which they occur. // Because of this, it is said that there are many figures in the camp of the stars, or because the future divine thing is not composed for everyone; for some are comforted in their heart, and others see truth by some sign that they see internally.

<meta>This page continues the technical discussion of astrological theory, specifically focusing on the "Centiloquium" or the "Hundred Aphorisms." It moves from the physical creation of talismans into the interpretative logic of the twelve astrological houses, particularly the twelfth house (traditionally associated with hidden enemies and suffering), and how the "angles" of a birth chart relate to the fate of kingdoms and rulers.</meta>

And some who are astrologers [state] in such propositions that the twelfth house <note>The 12th house in astrology is the "House of Self-Undoing," traditionally linked to secret enemies, prison, and death.</note> signifies death and hatred, first through a mediated truth <note>original: "mediatum retatem," likely *veritatem*</note> such as a manifest year; it does not signify punishment through its own sculpted [image], but rather signifies more of these things through its mediation. **Haly** <note>Haly Abenragel, a famous 11th-century Arab astrologer.</note>, **Abennohez**, and **Malmos** have cared for the placement of the mediation of homicide, because the first manifest [intent] of his own mind brings forth great things; those sculpted things are a great first principle and a strength of mediation. This is because there are philosophers who say much concerning those whose death the lover of justice has cherished, or through the malice of kings, or the hatred of the wicked, which ought not to move from them; and thirdly, through things that he was giving as a gift. He prohibits astrologers from doubting whether to take from the infinite, nor to be interrogated by them, nor would he care if he received from them, so that he might receive correctly the manifest year. Since astrologers rejoice that he might give, or now [give] concerning the husband of the superior; rather, the mind of the philosopher is to be punished by the lord or someone else, and for this reason, concerning astrologers, the memory of the wicked seems to distribute to you the proposed three dogmas.

**W**hen, by the promise of the heavenly bodies, others [seek] to drive out the stars, **Haly** desires to expel them. Others promise and marvel at the stars above all things, because in this world he operated through his own power, which is to say he fashioned it. It is a work together with what is hoped for through three true signs, through luminous first-fruits, through stars; we are able to say that they are figures because truly they were with the thief, the redeemer, the mother, and it enters into the misfortune of superficial things. But for those, the luminous things are at hand to us through the stars, through the figures of the three first parts, or through the false work; but in that movement they were in the twelfth [house] which was of the stars.

# Here begins the theory of the planets

<margin>
Apogee <note>original: "Aug", a Latinization of the Arabic "awj," meaning the highest point or apogee.</note>
Center
</margin>
The circle of the center, or the eccentric circle, is considered to be that which departs from the center of the zodiac and does not have its own center coincident with the center of the world <note>In the medieval geocentric model, the "center of the world" is the Earth.</note>. <margin>Apogee and the opposite of the apogee</margin> The **Apogee** is said to be the extremity of the line which is moved furthest from the center of the world; it is also called the *Aux* or the *longer distance*. And the part which approaches most closely to the Earth is called the **opposite of the apogee** <note>Also known as the perigee.</note>, or the *closer distance* line. There are, moreover, two places which are in the middle between the apogee and the opposite of the apogee, which are called the <margin>mean distances</margin> **mean distances**.
The Sun truly moves by its own motion from the west into the east in a circular path; the center, however, by which it is moved by its own motion, carries it so that everything is moved in a shaped sphere and its opposite. The world, however, follows an obedient rotation toward the west, equal through the day.
<margin>motion of the sun</margin>
The **true motion of the sun** is said to be the arc of the zodiac between a line going out from the center of the Earth to its location and to the location of the first point of Aries <note>The vernal equinox point.</note>, and a line going out from that same center to the end. The line of the two carrying lines, concentric from the center of the eccentric through the Earth of the Sun through the day.
<margin>the sun is</margin>
The **true motion of the sun** is called the arc of the zodiac measured from the center of the world at Aries to the line going out from the center of the Earth through the body of the Sun.
<margin>equation</margin>
The **equation of the sun** is the arc of the zodiac falling between the mean motion and the true motion; and then this equation, which for the Sun is zero at the apogee or at the opposite of the apogee, is truly at its maximum when at the mean distances. <margin>apogee of the sun</margin> Truly, the arc of the Sun's degrees of the zodiac falling between the mean... and the line emanating from the mean motion is the apogee of the Sun in its own [sphere].

<column-break/>

...signifying the degree of the zodiac falling between the head of Aries and the line which passes through the apogee of the eccentric. If the half is greater than the mean motion, the **equation** is then said to be an equation that must be **subtracted**. In the other case, if it is smaller, then the equation must be **added**. In the center, however, the mean motion of the Sun is... through the difference of the arc of the zodiac, thus it holds itself to the zodiac as it does to the motion of the arc... and it passes from the Sun to the center with the Earth in the rest of the planet, which is the distance of the true and the lower subject.

<meta>This page continues the technical description of the lunar model, specifically focusing on the corrections ("equations") needed when the Moon's epicycle is at its closest and furthest points from the Earth. Conversely, when the center of the epicycle is in the **opposite of the apogee** <note>original: "opposito augis," meaning the perigee, the point in the orbit closest to Earth.</note>, the timing according to the moon is then shifted. 
<margin>equation of the arc</margin> 
At the presence of the active center, the true and mean arcs are the same. 
<margin>equation of the center</margin> 
The **equation of the center** <term>equation: in medieval astronomy, this is a mathematical correction or "adjustment" added to or subtracted from a planet's average (mean) position to find its actual (true) position</term> is then at its maximum within the zodiac, according to the location of the mean and true motion, which is the equation of the center of the moon, etc. When the epicycle is in the apogee or in the opposite of the apogee, the line of the moon's mean center is at its furthest or nearest point, according to the epicycle of centers. Or, it is the equation of the center of the epicycle at its mean longitude. Nevertheless, for the moon and the line of the center, at the mean longitudes of the moon, the epicycle is half of the semi-diameter of the epicycle, which is the distance from the center of the moon. Then the mean motion is at its greatest, which is the arc of the center. Then the equation of the arc subtended is equal to some part or half; that is, near the more remote part by the equation of the center. This arc of the center is equal at the furthest point and the opposite of the apogee, and at the apogee, and in the diameter. These are the equations of the center for the arc of the epicycle's center according to the moon at the apogee; and when the center is at the opposite of the apogee, it is called the equation of the center. This is half the diameter of the moon's center [measured] by equal perpendicular arcs, which are written in the tables as equal, as if the axis of the epicycle were in the apogee of the moon's center. When the center of the epicycle is in other locations, the equation of the arc followed the axis of the epicycle as it adds to the center of the center; and this arc is called the equation of the center. It is decreased by **proportional points**, because the proportional points consist of 60 points <note>Medieval astronomers used a base-60 (sexagesimal) system for precision, much like we use 60 minutes in an hour.</note> of the moon, drawn to the center of the moon through the arc of the center.

<column-break/>

This is divided into 60 proportional parts. What is called the arc of the center at the opposite of the apogee has none of these parts; when it is at the apogee, it possesses others. In other locations, it possesses these proportional parts according to the different distance cut off from the apogee or the opposite of the apogee, according to the proportion shown in the figure.

### theory of the moon
### on the motion of the head and tail of the dragon

**Since** the moon deviates from the path <margin>head & tail</margin> of the sun in two directions across the middle of the world, and intersects that same path in two opposite places, it is necessary that there be two: the **Head and the Tail of the Dragon** <note>These are the lunar nodes: the "Head" (Caput Draconis) is the ascending node where the moon moves north across the ecliptic, and the "Tail" (Cauda Draconis) is the descending node where it moves south. They are essential for predicting eclipses.</note>. From the arc of intersection, the moon begins to decline toward the North, and the "Tail" is called the arc of intersection. These also move from East to West at a rate of nearly three **seconds** <note>original: "minutis secundis." These are "second minutes," or what we simply call seconds of a degree.</note> per day. This motion is said to occur over the long span of the world in whatever way the moon is equal to the centers in magnitude. It is located on the surface of the **circle of signs** <note>The Zodiac or Ecliptic.</note>, which is the path of the sun. This motion is different from the motion of the planets, because it moves from West to East, and covers its hours through the sun.

### What follows is on the theory of the three superior planets
<note>The "three superiors" refer to Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn, which are further from the Sun than Earth is.</note>

It should be noted that each of the three superiors has two **eccentric spheres** <term>eccentric: a circular orbit whose center is not the Earth, used to explain why planets appear to speed up or slow down</term> arranged in a flat and immobile surface, except through the motion of the eighth sphere <note>The sphere of the fixed stars.</note> and the daily motion and the earth <note>likely referring to the apparent motion relative to the observer</note> from east to west. Each of these has two centers, and in the superior part, the center of the **epicycle** <term>epicycle: a small circle on which a planet moves, while the center of that small circle moves around a larger circle (the deferent)</term> is moved from west to east. And there is another circle, the **equant eccentric** <term>equant: a mathematical point used to explain the observed speed variations of planets; the planet moves at a constant angular speed as seen from this point</term>, which shows the origin of the motion; at equal times, it describes equal angles at the center. In its other part, it is equalized on the plane. And that circle whose center is nearer [to the Earth] is called the **deferent** <note>original: "deferens"; the large circle that carries the epicycle</note>. Those which follow the three are distant from the others, and the one called the **apogee** <note>original: "auctio," likely a transcription of "auge"; the point in the orbit furthest from Earth</note> in time, and the center is called the **apogee**... which is in the middle, and these both are shown...

In time, it hastens and is equalized at a point in another place; the center declines toward the second point opposite the center of the eccentric, because the center of the world <note>The Earth.</note> is distant from the middle of the eccentric. For in these three planets, the diameter of the epicycle is equalized through the designated point of the world; then the epicycle’s reconciliation is in the apogee or in the opposite of the apogee of the eccentric. # On the motion of Venus and Mercury

And the mean motion <term>mean motion: the average speed of a planet if it moved in a perfect circle at a constant speed</term> and the mean argument <term>argument: an angle used to calculate a planet's position on its epicycle</term> and the equated center in the zodiac <note>original: *in zodiaco*</note> and the measured and equal distances and the mean and equated argument—all these are described for Venus and Mercury just as they were for the three superior planets <note>The "superior planets" are Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn, which are further from the Sun than Earth is.</note>. Otherwise, the epicycle is such that the equation <term>equation: a mathematical correction used to find the true position of a planet from its average (mean) position</term> is as was said, because through the furthest minute <note>original: *minutum*</note> are the equations, as if the deferent <term>deferent: the large circular path centered on Earth (or a point near it) that carries the smaller epicycle</term> of the inferior planets had taken all things with it. When, therefore, for the others, the epicycle [moves] in a great way... from above the star, it goes into defect, that which is before the epicycle... which is never produced... the same argument... those which are retrograde <term>retrograde: the apparent backward motion of a planet in the sky</term> are those which are seven... Therefore, the fourth in another part, then the epicycle moves smoothly in its own way, distinguished in another place at the highest point, then it will be known as in the first sphere... all are not so much spaces... as they are in the second sphere of longer longitude, and the epicycle is under its light. It is then said to the others that the epicycle, in its proper time, carries greatly to the line of the epicycle... by the grant of two dimensions in the second part. And the minutes of the sphere at the prior length are of the epicycle, they are in the second above... with the others as far as the sun is closer to the epicycle [moving] backward <note>original: *retro*</note> then. And from that same place as far as the apogee <note>original: *augis*, the highest or furthest point in an orbit</note> of the epicycle, since there is a line emerging which changes the minutes by its own diminution, or its diameter <note>original: *diameter*</note>. Then it is said that they should be described as they were in the three superior planets, but for Venus... seven.

<column-break/>

By this arrangement they know the three spheres and in the same place it is seen in whatever center of the sun the time of the epicycle follows... just as the sun is seen to be measured by the motion of the sun, which is the mean motion of the epicycle <note>In medieval astronomy, the "mean motion" of Venus and Mercury was considered identical to the mean motion of the Sun.</note>... from it two lines are distant... one is the center of the sun and the other is distant from the point through which the deferent goes. But they are equal and immobile, except that... the 8th sphere precedes, but the deferent moves in latitude <note>original: *latitudine*, the distance north or south of the ecliptic</note>... and from retrogradation, so that in others they are deferents and appear in the same flat surface under the ecliptic <term>ecliptic: the apparent path of the Sun across the sky; the plane of Earth's orbit</term>... only the deferent is said to be from the ecliptic. Concerning this motion, it is spoken of in the latitudes, and in other hours of Venus, they are similar to the three superior planets; and let what has been said of these things suffice.

### It follows concerning the direction and retrogradation of the planets

A planet is called "direct" when its motion occurs according to the common motion of the epicycle. It is in "retrograde" when its motion is not according to the motion of the epicycle. The "first station" <term>station: (Latin: *statio*) a brief period when a planet appears to stop moving before changing direction</term> is called the point of the epicycle in which the planet begins to go retrograde. The "second station" is the degree in which it begins its direction [forward motion]... it goes retrograde until that time, then according to the motion of the epicycle in this time, because by equal motion... the moon is distant in the upper part of the epicycle... and in the lower [part] it is swift... It makes the first station, which is signified by the falling of the retrograde epicycle in the apogee, as the epicycle... and the point of the second station... earth. For the two inferior planets <note>Venus and Mercury</note>, from the first station they are in retrograde for us... the first and second points mentioned.

**L**atitude of a planet is its distance from the path of the sun <note>original: *via solis*, meaning the ecliptic</note>. **Declination** of a planet is called its distance from the equinoctial line <term>equinoctial line: the celestial equator, the projection of Earth's equator into space</term>. Truly, because the sun has no latitude but only declination, therefore in the tables, the distance of the center of the sun's body from its apogee—or through the center of the sun to the tables of latitude—is taken from here. The distance of the center of the moon's body is taken from the first ecliptic which was in that line; with the sun's [motion] increased, the "Dragon" is taken, that is, the declination is taken in the two spheres of the signs in which the moon is located. And in the same hour, you take this latitude from the sphere of the signs, if the arc of the sun was away from it. But latitude and declination are either northern or southern, each according to how much we decline from the equinoctial. And if they are in different directions, we shall subtract the smaller from the larger, with the remainder staying in the part which was larger. And note that from the center of the moon, by its composition, it is distant from the path of the sun. And through this line, just as in the surface of the moon's eccentric <term>eccentric: an orbital circle whose center is not the Earth</term>, from here

[the Moon] has only one latitude, but the other 7 planets have two latitudes: one which is mediated by the epicycle or declines from the eccentric; the other from the eccentric which declines from the path of the sun. And through the tables, one may find information concerning each latitude, since through the table and through the table of the epicycle, the latitude is found by the center. And it must also be known that it has two [latitudes] in the eccentric which [move] toward the south; and so the table of the moon is made more for the half of the circle. And as for that part of the circle, that table of the moon would be more at 6 signs <note>In medieval astronomy, the 360-degree circle was often divided into 12 "signs" of 30 degrees each.</note>. <vocab>
**Latitudo (Latitude):** The angular distance of a heavenly body north or south of the ecliptic.
**Declinatio (Declination):** The angular distance of a body north or south of the celestial equator.
**Planeta (Planet):** In this era, this included the Sun and Moon as "wandering stars."
**Equinoctialis (Equinoctial):** The celestial equator.
**Sol (Sun):** The central reference for the ecliptic path.
**Luna (Moon):** The celestial body whose deviations from the ecliptic cause eclipses.
**Ecliptica (Ecliptic):** The apparent path of the Sun; the plane where eclipses occur.
**Draconis (Of the Dragon):** Referring to the "nodes" of the orbit; the points where the Moon's path crosses the Sun's path.
**Septentrionales (Northern):** Positions toward the North Pole.
**Meridionales (Southern):** Positions toward the South Pole.
**Eccentricus (Eccentric):** An orbital circle that does not have the Earth exactly at its center.
**Epicyclus (Epicycle):** A small circle whose center moves along the circumference of a larger circle.
**Auge (Apogee):** The point where a planet is furthest from the Earth.
**Caput Draconis (Head of the Dragon):** The ascending node where the Moon moves North of the ecliptic.
**Cauda Draconis (Tail of the Dragon):** The descending node where the Moon moves South of the ecliptic.
**Eclypsis (Eclipse):** The obscuration of one celestial body by another.
</vocab>

# Here begins the use of the instrument itself

If you wish to find, for this purpose, the true **conjunction** and **opposition** <note>The "conjunction" is the New Moon (Sun and Moon together), and the "opposition" is the Full Moon (Sun and Moon opposite each other).</note> of the sun and moon: first, seek the **mean motion** <term>mean motion</term> <note>The theoretical average speed of a celestial body, assuming it moves in a perfect circle at a constant speed.</note> of the sun and the **mean argument of the moon** <gloss>or one</gloss> <note>The "argument" is the specific position of the moon on its epicycle.</note> which is for that time. Likewise, seek the day and hours on the outer module, but on the line of the epicycle, find the point where the argument of the moon ends. Then, on the lower module in the **Zodiac**, find the point in which the mean motion of the sun ends at the time of the mean conjunction or opposition. After this, see if the point for the sun is further away from the line than the point of the moon's argument; if it is toward the left where the point of the moon's argument enters the spaces between the lines drawn from above with their minutes, then there are that many hours and minutes. Add these to the hours and minutes of the mean

**Right Column**

conjunction or opposition of the sun and moon. If, however, the point of the moon's argument is further from line A than the point for the sun, then the preceding two points [represent] that many hours and minutes. Subtract these from the hours and minutes of the mean conjunction or opposition of the sun and moon, and you will have the true conjunction or opposition of the sun and moon in hours. For when the moon is at the **apogee of its epicycle** <note>The "apogee" (Latin: *auge*) is the point where the moon is furthest from Earth and appears to move at its slowest.</note>, you have nothing in the argument of the moon. If, however, the moon is at the end of the apogee of the epicycle, then seek from the point of the moon’s argument in the interior of the epicycle what space in minutes [is shown]. The minutes will be cut in the tracks shown between the point of the moon’s argument and the apogee of the moon’s epicycle. Subtract that many minutes from each hour found through the aforementioned points. From these minutes of time, you shall make the reduction in this way: reduce the hours and minutes found above to the same denomination <gloss>namely hours</gloss>—that is, hours to minutes and minutes to seconds <gloss>minutes</gloss>. Having found this, reduce it again to the same denomination, namely to seconds. Then, let one be divided by the other, and by the remainder in minutes which is produced, reduce it to more precise fractions. These will come forth as the [correction], which you should subtract from the hours and minutes found above, and you will have the aforesaid **equated hours** <term>equated hours</term> <note>Hours adjusted from "mean" time to "true" time to account for the irregularities in celestial motion.</note>. These you should add or subtract as was said above, and you will have the true conjunction of the sun and moon or the opposition, as is clear in the following figure.

When you recognize these ten lines at their individual points, just as you do on your other most important instruments: this circle is depicted for you as a treatise on motions, marking the months through the second point. The second circle, however, with its markings and situated within the two solar **zodiacs** <term>zodiac</term> <note>The "circle of animals," the belt of the heavens divided into twelve signs through which the Sun, Moon, and planets appear to move.</note>—at whose joining [edge] the **epicycle** <term>epicycle</term> of the moon is located—the primary lines of the months are to be considered. 

But at the points A and B [the scale] provides the hours; note that it is not necessary to follow the order of the lines in this figure strictly, because for the sun there must be twelve [lines] for all the months, but for the moon there are more in the [southern?] part, because in the beginning of the months and by the calculation of the months, they are represented in a few points in the present figure. From the line that begins in **Cancer** <note>In this diagram, Cancer is positioned at the top, representing the Summer Solstice or the highest point of the sun's path.</note> at points B and C from the solar zodiac, the **meridian** <term>meridian</term> <note>The great circle passing through the celestial poles and the zenith of a particular location; it represents noon when the sun crosses it.</note> remains, and so forth; and both **colures** <term>colure</term> <note>Two principal circles of the celestial sphere that intersect at the poles: one passing through the equinoxes and the other through the solstices.</note> move from right to left with their titled numbers.

<meta>This page continues the technical instructions for medical prognosis based on astrological alignments, specifically focusing on the roles of the Ascendant, the Moon, and the "House of Death" in determining the course of an illness.</meta>

Regarding the evident specific judgments which pertain to medicine, it must be understood that for the successful outcome of these judgments, one must know the nature of the matter being questioned. The "good house" is determined by the **Ascendant** <note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the inquiry or the onset of illness.</note> and its **Lord** <note>The planet that rules the specific zodiac sign of the Ascendant; in this context, the ruler acts as a symbolic "physician" for the case.</note>, which represents the physician of the matter sought. One must also consider who influences the house by **aspect** <note>The geometric angle between planets; certain angles like squares or oppositions were considered stressful, while trines were harmonious.</note>, especially if they look toward the Moon and its ruler.

If a **malefic** <note>original: "malus"; usually referring to the planets Saturn or Mars, believed to bring hardship or corruption.</note> is in the Ascendant, it is a bad sign for two reasons, and it will cause no small harm to the patient. Consider also the **10th house**, which is at the **Midheaven** <note>original: "medio celi"; the highest point in the sky at the time of the chart.</note>. If it is well-disposed, the medicine will work well for the patient; however, if a malefic is located there, they make the condition worse. If a **fortune** <note>original: "fortuna"; a "benefic" planet like Jupiter or Venus, believed to bring health and success.</note> is present, it is a good sign in your judgment.

Signs of "fortune" indicate illnesses that are curable by medicine, whereas signs of "misfortune" <note>original: "infortunium"</note> indicate that the medicine itself will cause harm. Likewise, if the rising sign is **mobile** <note>original: "mobile"; also known as "cardinal" signs (Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn), which represent change and new beginnings.</note>, or if the Moon is in a mobile sign, the illness will reach its end quickly, whether for good or for evil. This is especially true if the Moon is joined to or aspects the Lord of the Ascendant. If, however, the signs are **fixed** <note>original: "signis fixis"; signs like Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius, which represent stability and long duration.</note>, the illness will be prolonged.

<margin>aspect</margin>
The illness will terminate for the good especially if there is a friendly influence, particularly regarding the Lord of the **house of death** <note>original: "domus mortis"</note>, which is the **8th house**. If the Moon or its ruler are joined to the ruler of the 8th house, or if they aspect it, it signifies the manner of death. If **Saturn** <note>Associated with chronic illness, coldness, and old age.</note> announces it, there will be no hope. 

Likewise, if the Moon is changed, and the Lord of the Ascendant is **moving forward** <note>original: "processiva"; direct motion in the sky rather than "retrograde" or backwards motion.</note> and increasing in light <note>waxing</note>, and both are in harmony and away from the malefics, then the patient will be cured in a short time. But if the Moon and the Lord of the Ascendant are hindered by the ruler of the house of death, it is a bad sign. If the Moon and the Lord of the Ascendant signify life, but the Lord of Death aspects them and weakens the Moon, these are great signs of death. When they weaken the good signs, it is a sign the illness will terminate poorly.

If the **Lord of Life** <note>The planet ruling the house or sign associated with the patient's vitality.</note> is in the **12th house** <note>Associated with hidden enemies and confinement.</note> or in the **6th house** <note>Associated specifically with illness and labor.</note>, these are conditions for which there is no medicinal remedy. Therefore, death is to be expected when the signs are weak and malefic. 

It should also be known that the first day on which the illness begins is critical. If the Moon on the first day is in a sign opposite to its starting position, it changes the quality of the illness. For example, if the illness of the master began with the Moon joined to **Mars** <note>The planet of heat and fire.</note> on the first day in the sign of **Aries** <note>A fire sign.</note>, it usually involves heat and dryness; but it may change into coldness and moisture <note>The four humors of the body—blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile—were linked to these elemental qualities.</note>. Similarly, if it began under **Venus** <note>A planet associated with moisture and coolness.</note>, the qualities shift accordingly. If the Moon is hindered or weakened on the first day, death may follow, as the Moon is the ruler of the body's life. On the **7th day**, the Moon will be in an opposite position <note>A square aspect, roughly 90 degrees from the starting point, marking the first major "crisis" in the illness.</note>, which further determines the outcome.

It emphasizes the "critical days" theory, where the Moon's movement through the zodiac signals shifts in the patient's humors and vitality.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the technical instructions for medical astrology, specifically discussing how the planetary qualities and the Moon’s position in different zodiac signs dictate the timing and effectiveness of treatments like purging and emetics.</meta>

Regarding the outcome of treatment; it must be known that when the signs and the **planetary rulers** <note>original: "dominis"; the planets that govern specific zodiac signs.</note> of the sign itself are strong, well-disposed, and favorable, then the suffering alone does not overcome the patient. A sign that is hot and dry, or hot and moist, is favorable <note>The four "qualities" (hot, cold, moist, dry) were the building blocks of medieval science, determining the nature of signs and the human body.</note>. In the opposition of hot and moist, the action of the disease is not as strong because the purging of the sign toward its primary state and its primary fortune does not act as intensely, and the **humors** <note>The four bodily fluids—blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile—which must be kept in balance for health.</note> are hot toward the end of a single day.

<margin>2nd point</margin> Since the matter is occupied in another sign, you should consider the quality of the matter; if on that day the Moon is in one of the signs of either quality that is well-opposed, it will be effective. If the sign is hot and dry, and it is a sign where the matter ought to be dissolved, the physician can work solo in Aries, for instance, operating by himself. On other days, when conditions are better and the influence is stronger, the prescribed medicines can work more briefly and effectively. A physician should be able to innovate in his work, and it is for this reason that astrology is necessary. Those authors who find it intolerable are mistaken, for they do not see that a practicing physician cannot please a patient in one place unless he is prudent enough to consider these greater efficiencies. Because of the movement of such a sickness, one must strive to understand it through the disposition of the Moon alone.

Therefore, when medicine is to be given, if the body’s **attractive virtue** <note>The biological force that pulls nutrients or humors into an organ.</note> is strong because of heat and dryness in the body, and the Moon is in signs where such a virtue prevails—namely hot and dry signs like **Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius** <note>These are the "Fire" signs of the zodiac.</note>—you will see that the Moon in a hot and dry sign strengthens the **expulsive virtue** <note>The biological force that pushes waste or excess humors out of the body.</note>. They say that when the Moon is in cold and moist signs, the "aspect" is not as effective. One should choose the movement of the virtues through the work of the medicine to comfort the expulsion. When the Moon is in cold and dry signs <note>Earth signs: Taurus, Virgo, Capricorn.</note>, its influence provides comfort and space for the treatment.

If anyone wishes to preserve their health well through the work of Physicians, they should ensure the Moon is in the cold and dry signs—though here listed as **Aries, Leo, or Sagittarius** <note>The text here contradicts standard astrology, as these are Fire/Hot signs; the author may be confusing the signs or the specific medical goal.</note>—then something can be achieved through the work, and the effects will match the name of the treatment. For the improvement of medicine, there are four virtues of **laxatives** <note>original: "virtutes laxandi"; medicines used to purge the bowels.</note> specifically derived from the aspect of the great planets. These should be timed so the medicines are truly effective, though they should not be too exposed. This is what is said about strengthening any medicine, which is why many physicians look to astrology. If one wishes to be purged by the greatest power, the physician operates while the Moon is in strong and moist signs, or "salivary" signs, unless another planet obstructs or infects the work.

It must be understood that different planets govern different humors, and one must pay attention so that when a certain humor needs to be evacuated, a time is not chosen where that planet is poorly situated or weakened. It should be known that:
- **Jupiter** governs medicine and many other things <note>Jupiter was often associated with the "blood" humor and general vitality.</note>.
- **Mars** governs **cholera** <note>Yellow bile, associated with heat and anger.</note>.
- The **Sun** governs the spirit and the **blood**.
- The **Moon** governs **phlegm**.

Furthermore, when the Moon is **retrograde** <note>Appearing to move backward in the sky; usually seen as a time of reversed or internal energy.</note>, it is good to give **emetic medicine** <note>original: "medicinam vomitivam"; medicine that induces vomiting.</note>. Let the cautious be warned: when medicine is given while the Moon is in **Leo**, it harms the stomach and the throat; it is not a good time for treatment then. When the Moon is in the "delay" of the signs—namely **Aries, Taurus, and Capricorn**—laxative medicine should not be given; instead, give an emetic. Note that the chosen time for medicine is when the aspects are favorable. If the **Lord of the Ascendant** is well-disposed, the medicine is better. If there is a bad aspect from **Mars** or **Saturn** because of the physician's imprudence, the sickness will stay in **movable signs** <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn; these signs represent quick changes and beginnings.</note> and pass quickly. If it is in **fixed signs** <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius; these signs represent stability and duration.</note>, the purging will be stable or of a moderate duration and will have its effect.
