<meta>This page continues the technical instructions for medical astrology, moving from the qualities of signs and humors to the specific calculation of the "Part of Fortune"—a mathematical point in a horoscope believed to indicate prosperity and health—and how to predict conflicts.</meta>

It should be noted that the Moon always [governs/rules]... which are the privileges of the laws of the earth and the...

---

<margin>
To find the Part of Fortune <note>original: "partem fortunae"; an imaginary point in astrology calculated by the distance between the Sun and Moon, used to indicate success and well-being.</note>.
</margin>

From this, they say that you should call Venus and Jupiter the "fortunes," and all others unfortunate. Others, indeed, place Saturn and Mars as the "minor misfortunes" under an equal temperament. Or, if you wish to calculate the **Part of Fortune**, which is very necessary for medications, consider whether it is before noon or at night. If it is during the day, calculate the signs that are from the Sun to the Moon; then take the degrees which the Sun still has to traverse in its sign and add the degrees which the Moon has already traversed in its sign. From these totals, add the degrees of the **Ascendant** <note>original: "ascū" for *ascendens*; the zodiac sign that was rising on the eastern horizon at a specific moment.</note>, and from the total, subtract [increments of 30] to find the sign and whatever remains. Once this is done, compute the signs between the Sun and Moon, adding the sign you found from the remaining degrees. Compute this in the tables...

<margin>18 Prepare</margin>
...in an unfortunate manner... the **Part of Fortune** where the degrees are: for example, the Sun is in [Aries] and the Moon is in 6 degrees of [Pisces], and 20 degrees of Cancer is ascending. Calculate the signs between the Sun and Moon in this way. Then take the 18 degrees that the Sun must still traverse, and add to them the 6 degrees which the Moon has passed; the total is 24. Add this to the degrees of the Ascendant, which are 20, making 44. Since a sign consists of 30 degrees, you have 1 sign and 14 degrees remaining. Begin counting from the Ascendant sign; thus, if the Ascendant is [Cancer], then [the next signs are] Leo, Virgo, and Libra. Since the sign is not yet complete in its degrees, the **Part of Fortune** must be placed there. For the night, calculate the degrees from the Moon to the Sun and you will find it.

# The Complete Book on the Judgment of the Stars

**Haly, son of Abenragel**, said:
Thanks be to the one victorious God,
honored, powerful, the author of nights and day,
the revealer to eyes and to purity itself;
may he remain wealthy and merciful, showing mercy
to those lords who have in their hearts the glory
of the kingdom; he who is supreme, may he always be
acknowledged. And after he had, without end,
determined the heavens and the hells,
he moves the stars, and with the heavens
working together, he suspended the earth;
and he increases all things which
the sight may reach; he looks upon
what is contained, and specifically on designated days;
and the sealer, the lord of lords,
by his own uprightness, increases and saves
his own, even those who let go of their faith in him.

<margin>This book <unclear>...</unclear></margin>
This is the book in which I have collected many
meanings for the mastery of the
science of the stars <note>original: "scientia stellarum"; this refers to astrology, which in the Middle Ages was considered a predictive science.</note> and of their
wonderful secrets; I have collected them from
the books of many wise men
and I have added to it that which I
myself have explained, as much through my intellect
as by my own opinion, and what I
found through wisdom. Since this
science of the stars is grand and
exalted, it contains much that cannot be
embraced except by him who is frequently
engaged in it; for which reason I have divided the whole
explanation through its different parts.

Because it is the science of the First One <note>Refers to God or the First Cause.</note>, it surpassed
both the gifts of the Lord God and the
secrets reported to such great intelligence,
often to those who are subtle and
shrewd, because these things are known through the intellect
and by their own subtlety and the sharpness
of their nature; those who follow the tracks
of one who passes through these things, if oppressed,
will fall into it and lose the path
of its majesty and its vastness.
And I have set down this book as authoritative and
complete, which receives
all the manners of this knowledge from the beginning
of its roots until the completion
of all its operations; for I
proposed in the beginning to speak of the signs
and their subject matter, such as nativities <note>Individual birth charts.</note>,
and of the planets and their
qualities, and of the times which cannot
be excluded; since by the command of the water <note>Likely a reference to the humors or the elemental nature of the signs.</note>
I shall speak in the judgments of the world.
I have spoken in "questions" <note>Horary astrology, where a chart is cast to answer a specific question.</note> and this
I have placed in three parts; furthermore,
I have spoken of nativities
and placed them in two parts,
which parts I have divided here in the book
for the sake of brevity. Afterward, I
spoke on the revolutions of the years <note>Solar returns or yearly predictions.</note>
of the native, placing them in one
part; and for that reason, there are
eight parts of the book, except if time
leaves them behind and there remain
five parts or five books.

<margin>This book <unclear>...</unclear></margin>
**The twelve signs** are
in the heaven, similar to the clouds
of bodies whose nature is clear
and substantial; these are the roots
of bodies, and in them is retained
the persistence of plants;
in their presence, entrance,
and exit from them, there are
diversities of times and airs, and
the coming of heat and cold.
The first lordship of the signs

**Leo**, **Virgo**, **Libra**, **Scorpio**,
**Sagittarius**, **Capricorn**, **Aquarius**,

### The Nature of Planetary Antipathy

He abhors <note>In astrology, a planet "abhors" a location when it is in "detriment" or "fall," positions where its natural energy is restricted or hostile to the sign it occupies.</note> and because his sign returns upon him, he abhors it. # The Moon

The Moon is watery and humid, and she is the lady of the world’s aspects. She is called thus by men because of her properties regarding the other things of time, her generations, and the specific qualities of her movements. With a "small hand," <note>This likely refers to the Moon's rapid motion across the sky compared to the other planets.</note> she travels and moves, receding from and returning to the Sun until she appears.
<margin>
Lord of the eclipse
</margin>
She moves along the path of the two nodes <note>The lunar nodes are the two points where the Moon's orbit crosses the ecliptic; eclipses only occur when the Moon is near these points.</note> against their positions. Eclipses can occur when the Moon and Sun are in improper alignment, as happened when they were in the water of the two nodes.
<margin>
Sign of the eclipse
</margin>
Because of this eclipse of the Sun and Moon, those who are present may seem lowly and vile.

In this astrological allegory, the Moon acts as the Sun's chief administrator.</note> is like a king’s official; when the King <note>The Sun.</note> grants power and a certain rank, he applies it wherever the nature of the Sun dominates. The Moon derives her light and her strength from him
<margin>
On the fortune and infirmity of Moons
</margin>
until she places herself in opposition. When she is in that place, the Sun resists her, diminishes her light, and takes back what he had lent to her. They placed this power in her possession, just as a king resides in his palace with his *Alghazel* and gives him strength and authority to command the people, to answer them, and to do what seems right to him. When the *Alghazel* is great in rank and it is the time of the king's business, he shares in the king's abundance; but then the king begins to diminish him and take away the high honors he had placed in his power. **Saturn** is a planet <note>original: "Saturnus ē pl[an]et[is]"; in the medieval view, Saturn was the highest and slowest of the seven wandering stars or 'planets.'</note> that does not hold a great seat for the lowly. The effects of Saturn

For the Sun provides him with heat and light, and yet he is the Sun's enemy, because his house is located in opposition to the Sun's. <note>Saturn rules Capricorn and Aquarius, which are opposite the Sun’s house of Leo on the zodiacal wheel, representing the elemental conflict between solar heat and Saturnian cold.</note> His primary nature is dark and belongs to the region of India. Insofar as he does not obey the heat of others, he is characterized as being covered by water, and by his own nature he governs perfected things. He is oriental in his position, and when he moves away from the Sun, he portrays himself as an "infortune" <term>Infortune: A medieval astrological term for a planet that naturally causes hardship, such as Saturn or Mars.</term> and a source of evil. This is because he is immune to prophecy and has the property of making things cold, even through his own freezing nature.

<margin>Saturn in Aries, 1st Face</margin> In the **first face** <note>A 'face' or 'decan' is a 10-degree division of a zodiac sign; each sign has three.</note> of **Aries**, behold the clarity and the painted greenness; he commends the mercy of God and philosophies.

<margin>Saturn in Aries, 2nd Face</margin> In the **second face** of **Aries**, he places enmity and wonder among men; he brings fluxes and ill will between one person and another, and manifests every grace of others as something foul, making them abhorrent.

<margin>Saturn in Aries, 3rd Face</margin> In the **third face**, he brings harm to feminine things; they trust in trees and in pleasure and firmness.

<margin>Saturn in Taurus, 1st Face</margin> In the **first face** of **Taurus**, there is a wild winter that happens to women and young boys, and likewise to young girls; in other fractions, it is better for those who are in debt.

<margin>Saturn in Taurus, 2nd Face</margin> He is condemned in a weary body and condemned in fortune; he emits voices to an idol beyond reason in every kind. He is of a bad quality, sad, sorrowful, and suffers the anguish of life.

**Jupiter** is the planet of quality, quantity, and goodness; he brings the improvement of the intellect, the senses, and of piety, through which he moderates and balances the person's fortune according to their appetite and body. He is of a noble and good nature, loving simplicity and chastity; he does not condemn or destroy, and he abhors suffering. His reason prohibits and withdraws the soul from its own evil works; he appears beautiful and is obedient to the person themselves. He is mild to the faithful and the law-abiding, and he approaches and reveals the piety of goodness. He prohibits and abhors evil and helps the poor. He is certain of those things which were predicted and gives a truthful account; by his good deeds, he is a peacemaker. He loves good and true friendship, completed without fraud. He is stout in body and limbs, appearing handsome to his brothers and in his works. He loves justice and detests [injustice]; he must see a thing before its goodness so that he may improve, strengthen, affirm, and verify it. If he must see a thing that is horrendous or evil, he withdraws from it, condemns it, and impedes it through his own power. His deeds are done with the good pleasure of God, and when he is strong, he is happy and firm, bringing fortune to the **native** <note>The 'native' is the person born under this astrological configuration.</note>.

<column-break/>

And he fulfills his works in the world. But if his influence is deteriorated (as when he is ill-placed at birth), he brings loss to the native, who becomes hopeless and lacks the utility of equity. Thus, he might give a "good" that is actually an evil of perfidy. Yet, by his power and his **aspect** <note>The 'aspect' is the angular relationship between planets, believed to transmit their influence.</note>, he can clarify the actions of the wind and the health of the rains. In the proper seasons, he brings a balance to the fruits of the earth and does not harm them; he provides equality and a copious, temperate space between the heat [of summer] and the cold of winter times. He minimizes infirmity and suppresses mortality. Whether in his general demonstration or his specific local influence, he provides strength in the mind and adapts the creature to the liberty of its nature, leading it to the world, to quiet, and to the air, liberated from the darkness of the winds. As God willed the pact to be made, **Thabit** <note>original: "th̄," referring to Thabit ibn Qurra (c. 826–901), a famous Sabian astronomer and mathematician who wrote extensively on planetary nature.</note> says that Jupiter was created from the quality of the air and pure light, and from true, clear, and purged love. He is moderate, masculine, and fertile. He signifies the day on which God willed to create the world <note>This refers to the 'Thema Mundi,' the mythical birth chart of the universe.</note>; he was then in the ascending house, with the Moon in **Aries**, **Taurus**, and **Gemini**. His light is diminished in **Leo** and **Virgo**, and he is obscured in **Libra**, **Scorpio**, and **Sagittarius**. His obscurity is further diminished in **Capricorn**, **Aquarius**, and **Pisces**.

<meta>This page continues the catalog of planetary influences, specifically focusing on the "Bestower" Venus. It transitions from a general description of Venusian qualities—such as music, wisdom, and temperament—into a systematic list of how the planet manifests when positioned in each of the twelve signs of the zodiac, from Aries through Pisces.</meta>

Venus is the bestower [of gifts] according to the time and the spirit received, and she is favorable to those who are near her. She is good for the will of wise men, for eloquent words, and for those who are free and gentle. She provides mastery and wisdom in action, just as she does in rejoicing, in singing, and in silence; she governs the continuous sound of horns and trumpets. She often allows one to beautifully perceive poetry <note>original: "metraey" probably from "metra"</note> and harps <note>original: "caprapas" likely "citharas"</note>. In any matter, she shows herself through words, possessing reason, purity, and the ability to teach or hold mastery. This is because she passes by the shore of the Moon <note>A reference to the proximity of Venus and the Moon in the celestial spheres</note>, unless she is unfortunate because of the malice that might be in her. Although she has a feminine nature, she rarely makes men effeminate; rather, she causes them to desire both women and males. When she is poorly placed, she causes an appetite for women that is without utility, resulting from a "split face" or a distressed appearance. Sometimes she grants sorrow over small things that happen, or great hope in the heart of the one born under her. # On Thought

Concerning thought <note>original: "cogitacione"; in this context, it refers to the secret intention or the specific subject a person has in mind when they consult an astrologer.</note>, and even concerning great thinkers about whom you might ask, and in what manner one understands it and what kind of nature the Lord has over him, he said:

<margin>Dorotheus</margin>
<margin>If you wish to know the rule for those who ask</margin>
Dorotheus <note>Dorotheus of Sidon was a 1st-century Greek astrologer whose work influenced almost all later medieval astrology.</note> says that when you wish to know the thought of the querent <term>querent</term><note>The person who approaches the astrologer with a question.</note>, look first to the lord of the triplicity <term>triplicity</term><note>A group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water). Each triplicity is ruled by a set of three planets.</note> of the Ascendant <note>The sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the question.</note>. And if it was in the house of its exaltation <note>A specific sign where a planet’s influence is most powerfully felt.</note>, judge the matter from its first place. If you find it in the "house of the world"—namely, that it was by its own will, in its own inheritances, and within its own terms—judge it by this, because of the place in which it will be, in whatever house it was. And judge by the aspects of all those lords. But if it was in a "pleasing" state <note>original: "placita"</note> in cadent places <note>The 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th houses, which were considered weak or "falling away" from the powerful angles of the chart.</note> or in places in which it holds no dignity, then do not judge by the place of the lord of the sign, but look to the planet that appropriates its own judgment over it—even if that planet does not aspect it, nor is it in another "pleasing" state—then judge by that planet and its place. And this will be the opinion of Hermes.

<margin>Hermes</margin>
Hermes <note>Refers to Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of the hermetic and astrological traditions.</note> also holds this, as do a great part of the ancients who followed him and compared it by the "third girl" <note>This likely refers to a specific "Lot" or "Part," a calculated point in a chart, perhaps the Part of Thought or Intent.</note> which...

<margin>Vettius Valens</margin>
Vettius Valens <note>original: "Vuellius"; a common medieval misspelling of the 2nd-century astrologer Vettius Valens.</note> says that to see the thought of one’s own will, look where the planet is from which the Moon separates, or from that which is opposite to it, or from that which is in the meridian <note>The Midheaven, or the highest point in the sky.</note>, and from which it proceeds in aspect or conjunction. And if such a planet is not found, look to the planet to which the Moon first applies <note>As the Moon moves through the sky, the first planet it encounters by a specific angle is said to be the one it "applies" to.</note> and judge by it. If it held any dignity in the Ascendant, such as being in the place where it is and having its own dignity, look not only to its own place but look to the house of another planet that might aspect it through its own terms and aspects. Otherwise, the thought of the querent is found elsewhere according to its magnitude.

<margin>Degrees equal in power</margin>

Namely, two degrees... in the length of the part from the head of Aries, are equal... and are the proper lords of the two degrees.

# On All the Commanded Signs

...equal in power. And because the signs concord in length, they are called equal in power <note>This refers to "antiscia," signs that are mirror images of each other across the axis of the solstices or equinoxes.</note>, and they have two parts because they have equal length. Of which two aforesaid... Aries and Cancer. And by the aspect of the planets and this property... in these places, and one is named such that in their aspects they are called "tortuous" <term>tortuous signs</term><note>Also known as signs of "short ascension" (Capricorn through Gemini in the Northern Hemisphere), which appear to rise more quickly and at a steeper angle over the horizon.</note> but...

<margin>tortuous signs</margin>
...with their own obedient rules, by the diversity of their aspects, they are more generous and free in giving fortune and are good makers. Infortunes <term>infortunes</term><note>The "malefic" planets, traditionally Saturn and Mars, which were thought to bring challenges or delays.</note> are prohibited by themselves from acting. And why? Because a fortune <term>fortune</term><note>The "benefic" planets, traditionally Jupiter and Venus, thought to bring luck and harmony.</note> which gives a certain thing, aspects it and asserts it.

<margin>fortune</margin>
And the infortune which gives a certain thing permits it to be taken away. The misfortune that happens from two infortunes which are in the same degree, and the equal fortune of two fortunes which are in the same degree, will not benefit in their terms. Just as the part of the septile of infortunes does not hinder, but like the opposite of the fortunes... the lunar... through two lords of the days and another of the night. For the fortunes are two: diurnal and nocturnal; the infortunes are two: diurnal and nocturnal. And in their terms, there is a middle ground which joins them in their own direction. Those mentioned are masculine, and those which are direct in motion <note>original: "rectigradi"; planets moving forward from our perspective on Earth, as opposed to retrograde.</note> are... properly from the manifest rule. Finally, because in a planet... masculine which rule over these, whether good or evil, it speaks of many things that come suddenly through Mars. And great delay comes through Saturn. That angle pronounces, and if they are fortunes it will be... free, and those who are in infortunes in their properties will be according to the aforesaid. And as for the nature of Mercury <note>original: "mercuriosa"</note>, those things which happen by accident possess the fact that they are fluctuating in property, as asserted by the signifier according to the house which it is in.

### Concerning the Dignities

The **dignities** <note>Essential dignities are the five ways a planet gains strength based on its position in the zodiac: House, Exaltation, Triplicity, Term, and Face.</note> are to be known here: the **House**, the **Exaltation**, the **Lord of Triplicity**, the **Lord of Triplicity**, and the **Lord of the Face** <note>original: "dominus faciei"; also known as the Decan, a 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign.</note>. And let it be that since the Lord [has] dignity, or two powers, or lordship of the face, and since in this kind of [chart] one should first look to the Lord of the aspect and give to it prerogative and strength. If the Lord is situated in the **Ascendant** <note>The sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the chart.</note>, which is said to have exaltation and the property of the face, it should be received as the **indicator** <note>original: "presignatore"; the planet that signifies the outcome or the person.</note> and by the name of the **Almuten** <note>original: "almubtez"; the planet that holds the highest combined score of dignities at a specific degree.</note> itself. No other [planet] will hold a division of the spirit's part <note>The "Part of Spirit" is a calculated mathematical point in a chart related to the Sun and Moon.</note>.

And if the Lord of the Ascendant does not come into any [aspect] of the four angles, and especially in the **Midheaven** <note>original: "medio celi"; the highest point in the sky, or the 10th house, representing career and public standing.</note>, then unless it has lordship by house according to the Ascendant, that planet itself is the indicator and no other part is preferred, unless it is from another planet which has exaltation in the Ascendant. And likewise, if there are manifest planets, then the participating planet will have [priority] with the Lord of the Ascendant in indication. This will be the case if the Lord of the Ascendant was not remote from the degree of the angle by more than 7 degrees.

If the Lord of the Ascendant was remote by more than 7 degrees, and another planet following in dignity was in that very degree of the angle, it will be stronger and its indication will be [preferred] in the matter. And if the Lord of the Ascendant had no dignity nor was in an angle, then the **Lord of Three Dignities** <note>A planet holding triplicity, term, and face, for example.</note> will be stronger than it by the fact that it stands at the beginning of the sign. Furthermore, if it was at the end of the sign, the Lord of two dignities will be stronger than it. For the Lord of Triplicity and Exaltation and Triplicity [is stronger], while the Lord of the Face is weak in this [regard], unless he should have lordship in the house in which the **Sun** is by day and the **Moon** by night, or unless he was the **Lord of the Hour**. And know that the angles are the roots of indications, and after them the Lords are stronger, and the weakness is [when] the Lord of the house is [remote].

<column-break/>

[This is determined] by the Sun by day and the Lord of the Moon's house by night, or the Lord of the Hour. When there is an equality of misfortune, the indicator will be the Lord of the Sun's house by day and the Lord of the Moon's house by night, as well as the Lord of the Hour. I do not see [a way] of recognizing the indicator in its motion until the indicators are established toward one planet, or toward two, or toward more than two.

Likewise, if there are two planets equal in strength and participating in the indication, and one is in doubt as to which will be the proper indicator, one should know to which the Moon **applies** <note>Application is when a faster planet moves toward a mathematical relationship with a slower one.</note>. If she herself was in the Ascendant in her own house, in which she is powerful, and if the Lord of the planet is more [powerful] by day, or the Moon by night, or if it is the Lord of a strong part, he has greater strength than the other, and he is the **Almuten**—especially if he was in the first hour.

Greater force is with the Moon when she applies to the Ascendant. Regarding the force of two planets, whichever was firmer will be the Lord, especially if the Moon applied to it. In the nocturnal houses of all, the same applies to the indicator to which [the Moon] applies in the indications, or to which she applies that are in the quantity of the light of the planets (which are their rays). One of the **malefics** <note>original: "infortunarum"; usually Mars or Saturn.</note> does not disturb and [remains] wise, and the Moon and the **benefics** <note>original: "fortunarum"; usually Jupiter or Venus.</note> make them hasten to have [effect].

As the Moon of the planets was, so the day is prolonged. **Antiochus**, **Dorotheus**, and **Duellus** <note>Refers to ancient astrological authorities: Antiochus of Athens and Dorotheus of Sidon. "Duellus" may be a corruption of Vettius Valens.</note> say that the Almuten is taken from the strongest appearing [planet] and from its Lord and from the place in which it is. And likewise for the Lord, that whatever planet places itself in the house of another planet, the Lord of that house will be the Almuten in that house. If it was in the degree of the Ascendant, it was in the arcs, and its Lord in the Ascendant [is powerful]. Or the Almuten is according to my method: if both of them are in the house of their second, and they were equal in their dignities, the firmer one in the house is the Almuten of them.

In the closer degree of the angle is the **Almuten** <note>original: "almutz"; from the Arabic *al-mubtazz*, meaning "the winner" or "victor." For I say thus: the affirmer of the houses, when he gives virtue to another part—that is, he who receives the **disposition** <note>The management of one planet's affairs by another.</note>—will be the Almuten. When I wish to say that the receiver of the receiver has it, if in this manner there are three or more, for that reason the receiver shall be the Almuten. **Application** <note>original: "Applicatio"; the movement of a faster planet toward a slower one until they form a precise aspect.</note>

Here it is clear: when one of them has more dignities in the Moon’s own place or its house, give to him the **Application** first, and to the other afterward. ### The First House

<margin>First house</margin>
The 1st House is the **Eastern Angle**. At the time of the thing's signification, it signifies the **querent** <note>The person asking the question.</note> because he acts for himself, his friends, his body, and the goodwill with which he seeks concerning himself. It signifies the newborn and his habits, colors, and his own things through his personal integrity in his shared clothes; and for how much time he lasts in the mother's womb. It signifies life, the nobility in which land he was born—whether there be an impediment—and concerning daily foods. The thing which ascends signifies to what degree that person ascends from common nature, his maintenance and his lordships; whether they be things of strength, of narrowness, or aspects in the face, marks, intellect, and his father's nature. And in common, the things of the ascending part are things of delay and from these things.

### Timing and the Arrival of Messengers

**Column 1**

If the **significator** <term>Significator: The planet in an astrological chart that represents the person or object being asked about.</term> is **retrograde** <term>Retrograde: When a planet appears to move backward in the sky, usually indicating delays, reversals, or a return to a previous state.</term>, he will return in the time that it takes for the planet to become **direct** <term>Direct: The normal forward movement of a planet; here signifying the resolution of a delay.</term>. In the number of degrees remaining until it turns direct, that shall be the time in hours, days, months, or years, and its significance is reached when it joins with another planet. Judge the matter accordingly. Sometimes the matter is disposed toward agreement, especially regarding **Venus** when she separates from **Mars** and the **lord** <note>The planet that rules the specific zodiac sign or "house" involved in the question.</note> of the person does not **apply** <term>Application: The movement of a faster planet toward an aspect with a slower one, indicating a future event.</term> to him on the day that precedes him. And if you have received two [planets], they are at least toward the **house** <note>One of the twelve divisions of the zodiac representing different areas of life; the "House of Mars" refers to Aries or Scorpio.</note> of Mars; the same will be said for me in the house of Mars concerning the one who sent him. 

And if it is asked concerning a **messenger** <note>original: "nuncio"</note>, whether he comes or not: look in this to the **Moon**. If she is applying to **Venus** or is in the **Midheaven** <note>original: "medio celi"; the highest point in the chart, representing success and public arrival.</note>, judge that the messenger is coming. And if the Moon moves in the **fourth house** or if she applies to the degree of the **Ascendant** <term>Ascendant: The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the question, representing the "now" or the beginning of an event.</term> or another of the four [angles], judge similarly that he comes. Let the Moon be in any month; if she is as described, judge more surely of the arrival of the messenger, and that the messenger is on the journey and will come quickly. 

But if the Moon moves in the **twelfth house** <note>The house traditionally associated with hidden things, delays, or confinement.</note>, casting her rays to the **querent** <note>original: "aspitantem"; the person asking the question.</note>, and she is entering [a sign], look to the twelfth part, for she will more likely deny the arrival. From this same hand, judge the haste, for the Moon is easy to reach in this matter. These things are through the **lord**... and through the least which do not appear to the querent; while looking, judge that the messenger is not coming. 

When, however, it is asked if the messenger brings the thing for which he was sent or not: look to the Moon and the **lord** of the person. By them, refrain [from judgment] unless one of them is separated from some planet whose nature is pleasing to the birth of that thing for which he was sent. And if that **significator** was under those planets, and after its separation from it, if it applies to the degree of the querent or to the **lord** of the querent, judge that this messenger brings

<column-break/>

the thing for which he was sent. And in this, look through the **application** of another planet to this matter, and you will be certified in this.

**O** When you are asked if **news** <note>original: "aqua"; though it literally translates as 'water', in this context of 'cartis' (letters) and 'nunciis' (messengers), it likely refers to 'liquid' news or is a scribal error for 'aliqua' (any news).</note> arrives, whether there is good or evil in it: look to **Mercury** and from whom he is separated. Because of an **infortune** <term>Infortune: A malefic planet, such as Saturn or Mars, believed to bring difficulty or bad news.</term> of the day, evil comes in the **letters** <note>original: "cartis"; literally 'papers' or 'charters'.</note>. And if a **fortune** <term>Fortune: A benefic planet, such as Jupiter or Venus, believed to bring positive outcomes.</term> indicates an extraction, it causes good or evil to endure through that matter, depending on the nature of that planet from which they arrive and its place in the signs and its state in the **Ascendant**. This is why it will have more dignity when it appears to him.

When you are asked for messengers, if one will come: look in this to **Mars**, since he is the **significator** of arrival; he runs through the messenger according to his movement into his **dignity** <term>Dignity: The strength of a planet based on its position in the zodiac.</term>. If the significator of the house sought on this day comes to the querent and <unclear>reaches</unclear> the place at the time he arrives, as he applies, look to **Mercury**, who applies to the querent degree by degree toward the degree of the **Ascendant**. And if he beholds him on that day, he will certainly arrive on the day of application, and more closely if that application was from an **angle** <term>Angle: The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the most powerful points in a chart.</term>. 

If Mercury has any dignity in the **aspect** <term>Aspect: The geometric angle between planets, which determines how they interact.</term>, you should know that such a messenger [is coming]. Or [look] to the Moon; if she is not appearing as the significator, say that he will certainly not come at this time. And if Mercury does not appear as the significator, nor has he in his place a part of the testament, judge that he will come slowly, and it will be at the time when Mercury applies to the significator degree by degree. And according to the favor of Mercury looking upon [the chart], and the Moon being separated from Mercury, then she certainly comes on that day when the Moon will be in the degree of the **Ascendant**. According to the movement of Mercury separating himself from two and applying to two by aspect, or to the same degree of aspect, or the degree of the significator, which is the **Alumbrez** <note>transcription of an Arabic astrological term, likely 'Al-mubazz', referring to a planet that wins a 'victory' or has the most strength in a specific degree.</note>, let it be judged.

Look to the **Almuten** <term>Almuten: The planet that has the most essential dignity and strength at a specific degree in the zodiac.</term> over the Sun and over the Moon, and while looking at the **Part of Fortune** <term>Part of Fortune: A calculated point in a chart representing health, success, and well-being.</term> and the Lord of the Hour, take the one among them that is the strongest in the figure as the **pledge** <note>original: "pignatore"; the primary indicator or significator</note> of the sick person. From the **6th House** <note>Traditionally the house of illness and labor.</note> and its Lord, and the application of water <note>original: "aplta aqua"; possibly referring to the quality of the 'humors' or the state of the planetary aspects</note>, his illness which he holds shall be known. From the **8th House** and its Lord, you shall know of his death. From the **12th House** <note>The house of hidden enemies and suffering.</note> and its Lord, and from the Lord of the Lord of Death, you shall know the end of his life.

Next, from the degree of the **1st House** <note>The Ascendant, representing the physical body.</note>, you shall know whether it is death or the cause of things. If you find the light and the stars are influenced by good planets rather than unfortunate ones, and their two **lords** <note>original: "abos"; likely referring to the two significators or the lords of the houses</note> are fortunate, he shall be saved from misfortune; judge then that the illness is in the **body** and not in the **spirit** <note>original: "spu"; referring to the soul, mind, or psychological state</note>. And if you find the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the House of light are both unfortunate, but the light and the stars are both fortunate and free from misfortunes, judge that the illness is in the **spirit** and not in the **body**. And if all are unfortunate and in misfortune, judge that the illness is in both—that is, in both the spirit and the body.

And **Masha'allah** <note>original: "mezehalla"; an 8th-century Persian Jewish astrologer whose works were foundational to medieval astrology</note> said that when the Moon appears unfortunate and not the Ascendant, the infirmity is in the body. And if the 1st House appears fortunate at the Ascendant and not the Moon, the illness will be in the spirit and not a loss of the senses, for these planets pertain to the spiritual matters belonging to him. And if both appear unfortunate, or without the **aspect** of a fortunate planet, the body will be corrupted and the sick person shall die. Know that the Almuten, who is the pledge of the sick person, shall be the indicator in this matter. See in which house the pledge was located according to the figure of the houses: the pledge of the Ascendant is the pledge of the **head**; the 2nd House, the **neck**; the 3rd, the **hands and shoulders**; [the 4th], the **chest, lungs,** and that which it contains within it; the 5th, the **heart, liver,** and the stomach; the 6th is of the **belly and the intestines** and the lower parts of the children

[of the body]; the 8th is of the **private parts of women and the testicles of men**, the bladder, and the thighs; the 9th is of the knees; the 10th of the shins; the 11th of the ankles; and the 12th House is the **indicator of the feet**. And in whichever of these houses the pledge is found unfortunate, judge that the illness is in that limb. And the nature of the house and the planet making it unfortunate shall also be considered, even if it appears with a better aspect.

And if you wish to know on which side of the body the illness is, look simply at the unfortunate significator; if it is above the earth <note>Above the horizon in the astrological chart.</note>, say it is in the **right side**, and if it is below the earth, say it is in the **left side**. Alternatively, look at what degree the Ascendant is in, look at the equal degrees and multiply them by the 12 signs; and the number that comes from there, starting from the degree of the Ascendant, divide by 30 degrees for each sign, and in the place where the number is, there is the illness in that limb, beginning with the head in Aries according to the order of houses which we have already spoken of. ### Concerning the slowness and return of the journey

Talking about the slowness and return on the journey, the chart indicates if the person will stay for a short time in a **movable sign** <note>original: "mobili"; The movable or 'cardinal' signs are Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn, which suggest change, movement, and new beginnings.</note> and if he will return quickly, or if the journey itself will be changed for another. If there is an opposition, it signifies weaknesses, prayers [for help], and obstacles to safety. For the most part, business will be weak and there will be hindrance through slowness and obstacles in his deeds. However, when the **Lord** <note>original: "dominus"; the planet that rules the specific astrological house or 'lot' governing the journey.</note> has been a **Benefic** <note>original: "fortuna"; literally 'a fortune,' referring to 'good' planets like Jupiter or Venus which bring positive outcomes.</note> by aspect, or if it was in the house of trust or opposite to it, there will be improvement and prosperity for the journey and its business, and it will be easily completed. 

If there is visible help, he will have guidance, whether good or bad as it appears. Look to the planet’s aspect and to which planet the **Significator of the Journey** <note>The specific planet representing the trip in the astrological chart.</note> is **applying** <note>original: "applicat"; an 'application' occurs when a faster planet moves toward a specific geometric angle with a slower planet.</note>. If it indicates prosperity, it will be in the return of the journey. If the application is away from the one the significator is **separated** from, it will be good and prosperous at the departure and at the beginning of the journey. 

See if the sign is **fixed** <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius. These signs represent stability, endurance, and slowness.</note>; then nothing will change for a long time, but it will improve in the land to which he goes. If it is a **common sign** <note>original: "commune"; also known as 'mutable' signs—Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces—which represent transition and flexibility.</note>, he will soon move from one place to another. If it is a movable sign, he will stay in that land and on the journey for a moderate amount of time and return quickly. 

See if the Significator of the Journey is **retrograde** <note>original: "retrogradi"; when a planet appears to move backward in the sky, often interpreted as a sign of delay, reversal, or things not going as planned.</note> and applying to the Lord. If both are retrograde, or if the Moon or a retrograde planet sees them, it signifies the journey will be disturbed and fail, and he will return before he reaches the land he wished to go to.

<column-break/>

If the planet signifying the obstacle and destruction of the journey is a **Benefic**, it signifies that the disturbance itself will be for his own good. But if it is a **Malefic** <note>original: "infortuna"; literally 'a misfortune,' referring to 'difficult' planets like Mars or Saturn.</note>, it will be for evil and loss. Whether that good or evil occurs depends on the nature of the planet signifying the destruction of the journey, its own nature, and the house in which it is placed in the chart. 

And if the Lord is a Benefic and receives the Lord of the aspect in a friendly way, it indicates he will receive good from the **official** <note>original: "agente"; the person acting as an agent or representative of authority in that location.</note> of the land to which he goes, rejoicing with them, and that the official will favor him with a good spirit and gratitude. If there is no **reception** <note>An astrological condition where two planets are in each other's signs of dignity, suggesting mutual support or cooperation between the people those planets represent.</note> between the Lord of the aspect and the Lord [of the journey], but the Lord is with a Benefic, it may still happen that the official of that land will show him grace and double his favor. 

If the Lord of the aspect receives the Lord [of the journey], he will receive good from him, and this will be by the good pleasure of God and because of the love he has for them, and they will do this of their own will. But if the Lord is a Malefic and in an aspect of envy <note>Likely referring to a 'hard' aspect like a square or opposition, which suggests conflict.</note>, or if he is joined bodily to the Lord of the aspect, it signifies he will receive evil from the official of that land; and that evil will be of long duration and according to his power and country. 

If the Lord is a Malefic and the Malefic is the Lord [of the destination], the lord of that land will suffer evil in his money, and that evil will match the nature of that Malefic planet and his state and power. If the land is a Benefic sign, he will receive good from noble and famous people. If he enters among those who are flourishing, it signifies it will be auspicious and he will be protected in the land to which he goes; and this will be by all legal and powerful men and all the wealthy in that land.

### On dreams

<insert>77</insert>
The science of dreams is divided into three parts. One is natural, proceeding from one's own nature and gifts, or from the virtue of the planets, or from the **humors** <note>original: "humoriby"; the four fluids of the body—blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile—thought to determine health and personality</note> of the body. Another is that which occurs through divine obedience, which is **divine prophecy** <note>original: "divina pphie"</note> and the glory of God, which comes upon chosen men. The third comes from the virtue of the planets, which imposes many things that all men see, which are found to be perfect. This happens at certain times when they reach specific places and the bodies that hold power in the figure <note>original: "figura"; the astrological chart</note>. 

The third kind [of dream] proceeds according to the humors of the body. These demonstrate their cause by what is in excess. If a man has an abundance of **choler** <note>original: "colera"; yellow bile, associated with fire</note>, either in quantity or quality, then that man will see fires and flames. He seems to see waters [if phlegm is in excess]. If **melancholy** <note>original: "melancolia"; black bile, associated with earth and heaviness</note> is seen, it is because he is in darkness, or feels he is carrying heavy weights. In the **blood** <note>original: "sanguine"</note>, the dream follows the humor that impels him. What is in the body or nature is perfected by the wisdom of the man; then also by the power that comes from the planets. This third kind of dream can be either an empty error or a truth, because they propose what is to come and reveal it.

### Here begins the seventh book on elections

Just as I have held in this book, having approached all the doctrines of the stars and seeking the principles and administrations and tables to the best of my ability, my discourse has touched upon what the ancient wise men disputed. For example, Ptolemy <note>Claudius Ptolemy (c. 100–170 AD) was the most influential astronomer and geographer of antiquity, whose work formed the basis of medieval astrology.</note> wrote regarding elections <term>elections</term> <note>Electional astrology is the branch of the craft used to determine the most "fortunate" moment to start a project, such as a war, a marriage, or a journey.</note>, because there are those who affirm them, and those whom the stars prohibit, and there are those

<column-break/>

who deny them and doubt. Through this I have proposed indications and the reasons for each, and they have explained their disagreements and their own [theories]. At the beginning of this book, in the first part, I showed these things, and in this place, concerning their lines, I wish to say that which I believe concerning their sayings; it is true and perfect, and here I begin it with the help of God.

Truly, because concerning elections, some are profitable by the help of God or His aid, and it is manifest that they exist and they know the way. There are others that are not apparent, which suddenly snatch away the words of the <unclear>p[ro]hiecarum</unclear> <note>Perhaps "prophetarum" (prophets).</note> which are lost in the proposed utility. Rather, it is more manifest and firm whether a man shall have a son, or if he shall not have one, or whether he shall live <note>original: "uinet"; likely a scribal error for "vivet" (will live).</note>, or what the days of life are which are lords. And through the property of others they are condemned, as they are in the utility of the lord, and through the work, or when they are doubled.

Just as by those coming [to be] and other signifiers that have been misused in their houses or in other forms, remembered from the aspects of the performer. As misfortune leads, and lords are joined in natural unity and the signifiers in the house of condemnation, some [fortune] was condemned in the root <term>root</term> <note>original: "radlicitate"; referring to the "radix" or the natal chart, which serves as the foundational "root" for all subsequent astrological predictions.</note>. To know what you call from the signs and the **directions of the Ascendant** <term>directions of the Ascendant</term> <note>original: "directoria ascendentis"; a technique used to predict future events by "moving" the degree of the zodiac that was rising on the eastern horizon at a specific moment.</note>, of which that which is seen is not durable. <note>large ornamental red initial S</note> It should be known that regarding the entering of water, and in journeys by water, and in the entering of a ship, it is [essential] for the sea to have many of the aforesaid [conditions]; now, and following the "root" of the election <note>term: "election" — the practice of choosing the most favorable astrological time to begin a project.</note>, and another for the same reason, because it is a matter that cannot be overlooked regarding this hidden part, as if to avoid it. And I have seen other ships to which horrors always happened because of the contrariety of the winds, or for <unclear>obmaderimentis</unclear> <note>Possibly referring to shipworms, fouling, or hull obstructions.</note>, or for other new occasions that happen at sea; and other ships that were detained and perished, and those who go in them. **Bedelabbia** <note>original: "Bedelabbia," from the Arabic *Sa'd al-Akhbiya*, meaning "The Luck of the Tents."</note> from 8 degrees and 34 minutes of Aquarius up to 21 degrees and 26 minutes of the same. The Indians say that when the Moon is in this mansion, it is good for besieging towns and castles, for scouting routes, and for <unclear>breaching</unclear> walls and doing harm to them. Otherwise, it is good for hiring one's servants, because they will be strong, loyal, and good. Buildings that are completed during this time will reach their conclusion and be durable. It is good for those traveling by sea, except that it will be delayed. It is bad for partnerships because it leads to a bad end and loss, though a fugitive may escape.

->**Ptolemy wishing to know**<-

**P**tolemy, wishing to know the length of the habitable earth, began from the Fortunate Isles <note>The Canary Islands, the traditional western limit of the world in ancient geography.</note> which are in the Roman Sea <note>The Mediterranean.</note> in the West, [measuring] if you wish all the way to the end of the earth in the East. The Persians and the Indians <note>original: "parsi 7 iudi" (likely "Indi"); medieval texts often grouped Persian and Indian astrological traditions together.</note> say that the world was divided into twenty-eight parts by the quadratures of the planets, as has been said, and that each should have its portion toward Rome. Likewise, they say that in a climate <term>climate</term> <note>original: "climate"; ancient geography divided the world into latitudinal bands or "climates" based on the length of the longest day.</note> there are more or fewer capital cities which have a planet as their lord, or two houses <term>houses</term> <note>original: "domos"; the zodiac signs ruled by a specific planet.</note>. And in a climate with more or fewer joined cities, one might have one house, and in many other cities and capitals—totaling 21,600 in number across the whole of the heavens. Hermes said <margin>not a wonder</margin> <note>original: "nō mīa"; possibly "non mira," meaning "no wonder" or "not surprising."</note> that the number of these souls returning to God will be the number of all men upon the earth: 466,760,000,000 <note>The manuscript lists a very large, specific number regarding the population or cycle of souls.</note>, since one follows after another.

# Here begins the book of Abu Ma'shar
# on the conjunctions of the planets
# and what they signify

Note which planets are involved in the conjunction: namely the three superior planets, <term>Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars</term>. The "Greater Conjunction" is the second type; the "Greatest Conjunction" is when all three are joined together at once. This occurs when two masculine planets are among the greatest things, owing to the slowness of their motions. The sign that will appear, perhaps through an <term>evil aspect<note>An "aspect" is the angle planets make to one another; an "evil" or "malefic" aspect like a square or opposition was thought to bring hardship.</note></term>, causes the consuming of kingdoms and their transformations, shifting them toward fortune or its opposite. They cause destruction and signal the perishing of many things the earth has produced, such as the grass and the fertility of the soil. This also applies to matters of fire. If any of these cause rain and waters, there will be great variety and strength in the sea, with fluctuating depths and turbulence in its management, leading to scattering. In the middle of these regions, the Great Conjunction and other signs will cause disturbances in the earth and all things will be perplexed. Perhaps it will be better for the state of safety and for finding peace, yet it will also bring tribulations. This fear will cause the plants to be lost, and through the appearance of others, it will bring death and evils to all. There will be rains, snows, atmospheric tempests, and wars; such is the generation of events when there is gravity.

<column-break/>

The dignity of the Saturnian nature resides in a single kingdom, and the situation will endure until it generates another turn. When this occurs in the summer, it brings dryness to the earth and the air with great winds. In the autumn, there will be unequal snows and rains, and in the lands, there will be frost and cold until the next generation of time. Here again, it announces for whom these things shall be, whether adverse or otherwise. For if the **Moon** is at rest, yet possesses most unfortunate qualities, we must provide various herbal medicines so that she might assist in great and dangerous works. And if the state of the air becomes known—whether it be rain, or if it occurs during the <term>harvest<note>original: "messione"</note></term>—it brings utility in the winter, though also many inequities.

If, however, the **Moon** is joined to **Jupiter**, then there is good fortune and <note>original: "phimoterio"</note> success in other works, especially if the Moon is manifest in the middle of the sky. According to the change of peace, it makes the air hasten; in matters of inquiry, it brings moisture and sweet rains, if the tempest allows. 

But if the **Moon** is joined to **Mars**, then it is a matter of chance, and by no means should <insert>the harvest</insert> be granted. I know that showers are provided; if it gathers strength in humidity, there will be bound showers in diverse regions. The planets, through the rains in which they dwell, will then act as a part of the whole. 

If the **Moon** is joined to the **Sun** during a humid harvest, and the Sun applies itself to **Saturn** or **Mars**, great rains will appear. This proceeds through the regions and purifies the air of the world. In those parts, through the application of the "evils" <note>The malefic planets Saturn and Mars.</note>, no rain is given, but the air is clear; or conversely, they may give rain. But if the **Moon** comes into a <term>square aspect<note>An aspect of 90 degrees, usually considered stressful or challenging in traditional astrology.</note></term> during a humid harvest, there will be showers. If it is applied to a superior planet, there will be fertility and dampness, which is the greatest fortune for this time. Yet above the valleys in the surrounding area, there is misfortune, and more rain will fall in the middle of the religious regions. If it is excessive, the months follow toward good, especially through the middle...

### Here begins the book of Abraham the Jew, the subtle astronomer, concerning the revolutions of nativities
<note>original: "Incipit liber Abraham iudei subtilis astronomi de revolutionibus nativitatum." Abraham Ibn Ezra (c. 1089–1167) was a celebrated Spanish-Jewish polymath whose works on astronomy and astrology were translated from Hebrew into Latin in the 13th century and remained standard textbooks for centuries.</note>

Among the Jews, Abraham <note>Abraham Ibn Ezra</note> teaches that we consider the best aids of instruments for determining **nativities** <term>nativities: the astrological calculation of a person's birth chart to predict their character and fate</term> to be the **astrolabe** <term>astrolabe: a portable medieval "computer" used to solve problems relating to time and the position of the stars</term>. Through this, using the quadrants, the hour, the **straight shadow** <note>original: "umbra recta"; the horizontal scale on the back of an astrolabe used to calculate the height of the sun or stars</note>, the **turned shadow** <note>original: "umbra versa"; the vertical scale on an astrolabe</note>, and measures made by water clocks and such, one achieves a second level of accuracy. **Ptolemy** <note>Claudius Ptolemy (c. 100–170 AD), the most influential astronomer of antiquity</note> says that one must consider whichever planet has essential dignity <note>original: "estate"; refers to a planet's strength based on its position in the zodiac</note> in the degree of the conjunction <note>New Moon</note> or opposition <note>Full Moon</note> of the sun and moon that immediately precedes the birth. He proves that the degree that the planet has traversed can indicate the degree of the **ascendant** <note>original: "orientis"; the sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</note> or the **midheaven** <note>original: "medio celi"; the highest point in the sky at the time of birth</note>. Ptolemy proved this to be useful in many cases. This reasoning was tested through the discord of philosophers regarding the parts of the planets in their respective degrees. We have personally observed in many births using the astrolabe, noting the longitude in degrees and minutes, the visual days and minutes, and the altitude of the sun at the exact moment of birth. From this, we found that the degrees and minutes correspond to the degrees in which the planets are located, such as in the midheaven. **Masha'allah** <note>original: "messehallah"; an 8th-century Persian-Jewish astrologer whose works were foundational to medieval science</note> also says the conjunction and opposition of the sun and moon should be treated as a special hour; then, one calculates how many hours have passed from the time of that conjunction until the first hour of birth.

<column-break/>

<margin>The hour and the circles above the spheres</margin>
...and it stays from the preceding position, so that at that hour and according to those proportions, it is distant through the whole daily cycle. One must act as is proper for the specific hour. Because of this, we have often discovered that the location of the moon at the hour of mercy <note>possibly a reference to the time of conception or a specific astrological window</note> during the time of birth will be the degree of the ascendant. And in the calculation, the place of the moon at birth must be placed at the time of birth. For example, if it was in the eastern calculation in minutes, it must be moved according to its proper distance... such as 2, 9, 7 <note>astrological coordinates or ratios</note>. If the planet is at the beginning of the house, it should not lack a distance of equal degrees from it. Take the proper degrees and the hour so that for each individual day, wherever the hour was in the middle of the time, you may add the distance of the moon in the degree of the ascendant for the days of its delay. If the average delay was 12 hours and 3 parts, and the moon was in the lower calculation, it stands in the degree of the ascendant at the same distance as before. Since it arrives at the world, add 12 hours and 3 minutes to this. This is true according to the second birth, just as in all other planets which appear in the degree of the ascendant, which the moon occupied. At the appointed time, the sun will go out from its place... This is true according to Mars and the Moon, just as it appears that the birth emerges from the days of the conjunctions. Ptolemy says that the 97th degree in the house of the 7th planet can be found there, as it can be chosen or divided according to the aforementioned 7 equal degrees.

# Book of Elections

<image-desc>A large ornamental Lombardic initial 'R' in red ink. The body of the letter contains delicate white geometric and floral patterns, including a small cross-like shape inside the loop of the R.</image-desc>

You have asked me, my son, to compose for you a book on the choosing of hours <note>This is the practice of "Electional Astrology," picking the best time to start an endeavor.</note> according to the opinions of the astrologers. Because this is a task I have worked on every year, I have collected this book as the best among all those three that have come down from the ancient fathers. It is divided into two treatises.

The first treatise concerns the benefits of choosing hours for those whose nativities <note>Birth charts.</note> are known, so that at whatever hours they make their inquiries regarding the things they most desire, they may know which hours are most significant. This is written in the second treatise, which deals with particular elections, such as those regarding towns and cities, journeys, and similar matters in their proper order. 

We present this book to them in a clear order, so that in this volume, which we wish to explain, this book of elections may be set forth. It is not like the books of nativities in which we might differ, until we restore the true meaning of these matters which occur. These choices have been treated in the books of the scriptures so that they should not be overlooked. Let this treatise be sufficient, for this method of treatment will please you not a little once the book has been presented.

The first treatise contains five distinctions <note>Chapters or divisions.</note>: 
1. The first is whether the choosing of hours is useful. 
2. The second is on choosing according to the masters. 
3. The third is on choosing hours for those whose nativities are known. 
4. The fourth is the knowledge of whether that which is asked will end well or poorly, and concerns the choices made after an inquiry has been made. 
5. The fifth is in which hours we should speak, and how that which is begun in them is established so that it may be effective. 

**Distinction 1: Whether elections are useful.**

The works of the judgments of the astrologers <term>judgments of the astrologers: the practice of making predictions or providing counsel based on the movement of stars and planets</term> are certain, as has been proven by philosophers through manifest reason. There is a change or an influence upon the soul; one must wait until the child is seen to emerge from the womb, and from that day forward, the methods of astrology are applied. Astrologers have not indicated the specific property of the child earlier because the hour of conception can hardly be verified. Ptolemy, however, says that the hour of birth is the beginning. If this is so, then choosing an "elected" hour <term>elected hour: a specifically chosen time to begin an action to ensure a favorable outcome</term> corresponds to the evidence found in the books of nativities <note>birth charts</note>. Good things happen to those born under certain signs, and the astrologer pronounces future events based on those births. We say the same regarding the planting of trees, the sowing of seeds, and the construction of buildings; in every beginning, the "house" <term>house: one of the twelve sections of the sky in a horoscope, each representing a different area of life like home, work, or health</term> of the endeavor must be established.

All astrologers are in agreement, saying that one must choose the moment of the Sun’s entry <note>The Sun's entry into a new zodiac sign.</note>, for their fates seem to be good or harsh based on these births. It is more laudable and greater if it beholds the **ascendant** <note>The degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at a specific moment.</note>, and if it were looking from an **angle** <term>angulus</term><note>The four most powerful points in a chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses.</note> regarding the **exaltation** <note>A sign where a planet's influence is particularly strengthened.</note>, then it is even more so. Otherwise, it should be in the degree itself by the **property of the matter** <term>proprietas re</term>, just as the nature of the planet makes the matter appropriate. **Albugasor** <note>original: "albugasor"; likely referring to the great Persian astrologer Abu Ma'shar (787–886 AD).</note> said:

**When** we choose [a time] so that it beholds something, then it is more appropriate if it finds that which they behold, where its lord was, or if the **house of exaltation** is strong; and it should have some property of it. Or just as where the **Sun** and **Moon** are, if he finds the Sun or Moon, it is better than anything else in which there was nothing. And he says that just as a mind <note>original: "mens"; possibly "measure" (mensis)</note> that has drying water there when the planet itself was "bad" <note>an "infortune" like Saturn or Mars</note>. But in respect to the Moon, it is [required] that she not be with a falling respect, and in the same way, they are in a **mutual reception** <term>recipiatio</term> <note>When two planets are in each other's signs of dignity, helping one another.</note>. Albugasor believes the Moon should be placed with the lord because those things are heavy, or more so than contrary things. The aspects themselves manifest things and divide where you will find rest. However, one person elsewhere says it is more appropriate—following **Ptolemy** <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the foundational authority for medieval astrology.</note>—that the Moon is not as previously described, but is hot and fortunate like **Venus**, as Albugasor testifies

where he speaks of **peregrinations** <term>peregrinatio</term><note>A planet is "peregrine" when it has no essential dignity in its current position, like a traveler in a foreign land.</note>, deceptions, and errors. Yet they have prohibited the Moon from being cold and moist and having a hot and moist aspect. He sought that she should have respect over every **beginning** <term>innuu</term><note>original: "innuu"; likely a variant of "initium," meaning the start of a venture or an election.</note>, and she is above every beginning in her property. Therefore, we ought to place her in a place suitable to her; and when she has the same "fortune," she should behold—as they say—the Sun. Through that aspect, it will be better and more fortunate, which increases the appropriateness. Just as the place of their lords, which was in a mixed **election** <term>electio</term> <note>The practice of choosing a time for an action.</note> from bad things to fortunate ones. Similarly in the four places, such as the places of the prevention and the conjunction and of the Moon upon the earth, which was in the hour of prevention. If it were in the hour of prevention of the Moon in the eastern degree <note>the Ascendant</note>, whereas in the western degree <note>the Descendant</note> it gave [death]. He said when he wished to have the conjunction <term>quietio</term> regarding all things which are... and the preventions of the Moon were made between the prevention and the conjunction, it will be appropriated from that prevention. Therefore, it is true in every beginning and in every **nativity** <term>natiuitas</term> <note>A birth chart.</note> to intentively consider these conjunctions.

<meta>This page continues the technical instructions for astrological "elections"—the art of choosing an auspicious moment to begin a task. ...as in the **preceding syzygy** <note>original: "preventionem"; the Full Moon or New Moon immediately prior to an event.</note>, drawing out whether it is situated in an **angle** <term>angulus</term> <note>The four most powerful points in an astrological chart (the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses).</note>, or in a quadrant of an angle, or in a **cadent house** <note>Houses that "fall away" from the angles, generally considered weaker or less effective.</note> from the angle. One must consider what is in that degree of the **conjunction** <note>original: "coniunctionis"; the New Moon.</note> as they come forth, and whether they behold it in aspect with the **benefic planets** <note>original: "planetis fortunis"; usually Jupiter and Venus, which were thought to bring good luck.</note> or the **malefic ones** <note>original: "mali"; usually Mars and Saturn.</note>. One must look at the aspects and which planets behold that degree, degree by degree, or by some other aspect. Similarly, one must consider the places of the conjunction to see if the outcome will be good, and whether it has many aspects.

If there are impediments in the seventh house, then the thing begun will indeed be weak and unprovable. If, however, a **benefic planet** <note>original: "fortuna"</note> follows safely, the matter and its goodness and eventual outcome will be praiseworthy. This is measured from the conjunction or the syzygy until it meets the bad or the good—that is, the malefic or the benefic planets. Suppose the places of the conjunction and syzygy are in an angular quadrant toward a benefic, and the **Moon** <note>original: "luna"</note> moves toward a conjunction with benefics; this will be an evident and ultimate sign of **exaltation** <note>A state where a planet's power is greatly increased.</note> and praiseworthy health.

But if the places are as described, yet the Moon is separated from the benefics and mixed with malefics, the beginning may be praiseworthy but the end evil. Or, if the place of the conjunction or syzygy is mixed with malefics, but the Moon is separated from them and joined to a benefic, the evil will be less, and the matter will eventually become praiseworthy. However, if the syzygy and the Moon are both joined with malefics and separated from benefics, all things will be bad in the beginning and bad in the end. If the degree of the conjunction or syzygy is in the **horoscope** <note>The Ascendant or 1st house.</note> and its lord is in the East, or in its own house or exaltation, or in its...

<column-break/>

...**triplicity** <note>A group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water).</note>, then the lord of the matter being undertaken will be strong and prudent. Thus, through his own cleverness and prudence, he shall escape from the predicted evils. 

These conjunctions and syzygies also signify the timing of the things begun. If the lord of the matter is in the seventh angle, it increases what is said of the person's cleverness and prudence toward the end of the matter. If, however, the location of the syzygy is cadent from an angle, then the things begun therein will be bad or of a watery nature. 

Some scholars seem to prove that a matter reaches its height through the quadrants in the syzygies; they imagine that in the same way, a matter reaches either a good or an evil end. But we see things happen otherwise. For two things of the same kind begun on the same day may turn out differently: one may be good and the other bad. We ought to understand this from the specific words said at the beginning of the chapter: if the **elections** <term>electiones</term> <note>The practice of choosing a specific time to start an activity to ensure a favorable outcome.</note> of the person are good, they follow that same mode. 

This is what **Al-Kindi** <note>original: "Alchyndi"; Al-Kindi (c. 801–873 AD) was a foundational Arab philosopher and astrologer known as the "Philosopher of the Arabs."</note> said: good increases good. If the election was bad, that which Al-Kindi said was good will be diminished, and evil will increase. If the election was good, it will diminish the evil that Al-Kindi spoke of. If, however, the election is very bad, then what Al-Kindi said will double the evil and it will happen quickly. It is clear that a good election increases the good and organizes it. The place of the quadrants is more appropriate in this work than just the quadrants themselves...

Elsewhere it finishes: the Lord of the Fourth, as in the [previous] mentions, who was **oriental** <note>Rising before the Sun.</note> before its election in its own house, or if they aspect it with their gaze in the hour of the election, will signify the effect of the matter. If they are received and fortunate in the hour of the election, it will signify good; if the opposite, it increases evil. It adds to the good if the Ascendant of the election is signified as fortunate in the revolution of the Lord, because that fortune is in some **angle** <term>angulus</term> and placed in the

<column-break/>

ascendant, whether in the first, or the tenth, or the seventh angle, or in the house of the matter. In the **degrees** <note>original: "gratiib'", likely *gradibus*</note> of those signs which are strong, [we act] in matters we wish to happen quickly, just as with those of swift motion. And regarding the Moon in the inception... **Al-Khayyat** <note>original: "alchabaui"; Yahya ibn Ghalib al-Khayyat, a student of Mashallah and author on elections and nativities.</note> says that if we cannot adapt both the Moon and the Ascendant, it should be adapted by the Ascendant for all daytime [elections], especially when the Moon is below the earth. If, however, it is a **nocturnal election**, it must be adapted by the way of the Moon, and especially when it is above the earth.

Or, regarding the proportional aspects, one should not place the Moon in aspect with Jupiter <note>original: "Iove"</note> or any other planet in the hour of the election in a septile aspect <note>An aspect of approximately 51 degrees, often considered minor or mysterious in medieval astrology.</note>.

Regarding those who have thought about the safety of the world: it is pleasing because it is good, or at least it does not seem that the world's diminishing should be considered. For it diminishes something of fortune from its own good just as much as it diminishes from the evils.

And note that for those wishing to hinder another prosecutor <note>original: "pquatorē", likely "persecutorem"</note> so that a good outcome is placed for a battle or for a sale, one should not be hindered by anything that was strong in the birth chart, especially the **Almuten** <term>Almuten</term> <note>The planet that holds the most essential dignity (power) over a specific degree or chart.</note> over the birth.

Alchabitius <note>original: "Alchabat". They did this so that their election would be perfect, lest there be some flaw in that election which would hinder the effect of the matter. For this reason, astrologers say that the evils that are present in the birth chart can be changed or even annulled through a good election. It was a very important thing to observe the birth chart; if that is removed, there will be no utility, nor can it be judged [effectively] using the Book of Judgments.

# The Appropriate Time for War when Mars is in Cancer <note>original: "temp aptu ad bellu qu mars m p ♋"</note>

Free from the "evils" <note>Malefic planets, usually Saturn or Mars, that were thought to bring misfortune</note>, with the **Moon** indeed below the earth in **Cancer**, or in **Scorpio**, or in **Pisces**, so that if a fixed sign <note>Signs that occur in the middle of seasons (Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius), associated with stability</note> and the seven [planets] are above the earth and in **Capricorn**, it is good and falling <note>Cadent, or moving away from the powerful "angles" of the chart</note> as it appears to the wise; unless the degree of the Moon is near the body or the aspect of **Jupiter**. Nor should there be an "evil" planet in the middle of the **Ascendant** <term>Ascendant: the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the election</term>. Let the Moon be in the fourth phase from the **Sun**, fortunate, increased in light, and in an angle <note>The four most powerful houses in a chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th</note>, so that the angles are remote. Let the **Lord of the Ascendant** also be in the east, in his **dignity** <note>The specific sign or position where a planet has its greatest strength</note>, in a primary angle or in the house following an angle. Let the sign of the Ascendant be a water sign, made fortunate by the "fortune of the Sun," and likewise for the Moon; and the **Part of Fortune** <note>A calculated point in a chart representing prosperity and success</note> must be adapted by the agreement of those who, as judges, spoke... <note>original: "dicepasc galay," possibly a corrupted reference to Galen or an Arabic authority</note>

As for the Fourth [House] of the Ascendant, let it be in a sign, and if there are two angles in a nearby sign of the angle—specifically two fixed signs—it will be better. Let the Moon and the Lord of the Ascendant be in a fortunate angle, or let the first [planet] in the middle be strong through virtue, dignity, and swift motion. Let the Moon also be in her greatest motion, adapted to **Mars**; if it is for a war and if ships are to cross... let the Moon be like a harvest for the middle of the Ascendant in its aids. In all these things, if the adaptation of the Lord of certain things is as... it will be good. Because when the Moon has been recovered from the water of the "Tail" <note>The "Tail of the Dragon" or the South Node of the Moon, traditionally considered a point of depletion or misfortune</note>, a strong grief is praised; just as when the Lord of the Ascendant is going toward an angle. And we must descend to the Lord... and the location of the ships, and to these we should adapt more than to the cause; and for the cause of the poor, let the sign be a water sign. It is better that he has a "house" <note>A zodiac sign where he is the ruler</note> and that he looks upon the Lord of the Ascendant with a praiseworthy adaptation; and it is better that he who is unfortunate [malefic] be the Lord of the Ascendant, provided the Lord of the Ascendant is eastern, going toward an angle in some dispute of... elevated... while the Ascendant is... it is useful that the house of the Ascendant be in a fortune, passing through the house...
