And if there are two in the fortunate [houses] from the house of the Ascendant, he will have confidence that he will receive the captivity of rebellious enemies with the help of God. We ought therefore to adapt the **House of Spoils** <note>The 8th house, often associated with the spoils of war or the resources of the enemy</note> and its Lord, so that they are adapted to be of assistance. 

And it is necessary that the **House of the Midheaven** <note>original: "domū medice," likely a corruption of "medii celi," the 10th house representing victory and authority</note> be looking toward the Ascendant and have in it some dispute, such as the house of exaltation or another... let it look upon the degree of the [Part of Fortune] <note>represented by the symbol 🜔 or Λ</note>; nor should it have any dignity in water, because that cannot be done. **T**ruly, for any purchaser of an inheritance, let the **Fortunes** <note>Jupiter and Venus are the "Greater" and "Lesser" Fortunes, planets associated with luck and success</note> have dignity in the **angles** <term>the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses of a chart, which are the most powerful points</term>, and especially in the **Ascendant** and in the **fourth [house]** <note>The 4th house rules land, foundations, and hidden treasures</note>. Let the Lords of the **Luminaries** <note>The Sun and Moon</note> also behold the Ascendant and the fourth with an aspect of friendship <note>a trine or sextile aspect</note>, so that it may be in a balanced angle, and let not the lords of the planets be **retrograde** <note>appearing to move backward, which usually signifies delays or reversals</note>. 

**Al-Kindi** <note>original: "Alchindi"; a famous 9th-century Arab philosopher and astrologer</note> said <note>The following line is a string of dense scholastic abbreviations: "h° s̃ p t̃ i m d̃ g q̄ ut m n̄ m uict m"</note> that the Fortune of the house should also be such that it is not burned <note>original: "i uisā" for "invisa" or "inusta", meaning "combust" or too close to the Sun</note> nor with interfering planets, especially if they are falling away from Fortune.

The **Ascendant** also appears changed if it was another watery sign. And if the Lord of the **Midheaven** <note>the 10th house, representing the highest point in the sky</note> be a Fortune, the Ascendant will be bad <note>the text likely implies a conflict between the owner and the land's output</note>. For the [fourth house] and its Lord signify the land itself and its possessor, as well as its utility and its expansion. But the Midheaven and its Lord signify whatever is produced from the surface of the earth, such as **trees, fruits, timber, and forest**. And its Lord signifies the cultivator of all these things. 

It is also found that when it signifies the libations <note>perhaps referring to yields or liquids</note> and other things which are not in that land, and its Lord is said to signify them by his goodness. And whatever is held in that [land]—just as a guardian might never find it good—is seen to be good in those things that happen. **Jupiter** and **Fortune** from which it is restored are united for the purchasers. Also, the Moon with the Master of the land signifies whether it is true, and to what the depths of the inheritances will come.

Observe that the Moon should be in reception from a Fortune, and she herself and the one who receives her should be in **Taurus** or in the following signs. Let also the Lord of the Ascendant be in the part of the Moon's labor; this means that the water of Fortune should be free in the house of the land, and [so should] the Lord of the **Part of Fortune**. And **Al-Kindi** said either the Lord of the house or for this part. He also said that for whatever degree, as in the "preventions" <note>likely "conjunctions" or "syzygies"</note>, let it be in an angle or falling toward the angle of the house. Whenever there is a Fortune in the house of "preventions," it is no

### Buildings and Mills
If you wish to play <note>likely "to build" or "to set in motion"</note> so that the aspect is in an equal sign like **Libra**, or in the final part of **Virgo** and **Pisces**, one must beware of the Moon in **Cancer** or **Capricorn**, because those are the quarters where the quality is said to descend and the nights among them are unequal. And let the Moon and the Lord of the Ascendant be in other signs without an aspect of an **Infortune** <note>Mars or Saturn</note>; this will be good. 

If it should be a **mill** placed upon **ships of the sea** <note>refers to "ship-mills," watermills built on floating pontoons moored in rivers</note>, this work is particularly distinguished. In a wall, the hand is required, except that a mill is more suitable according to where it will stand in that place. It is also good for those mills made of plates.

If [the sign] is a **movable sign** <term>A "cardinal" sign (Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn), associated with change and starting things</term> and the Lord and [the Moon] were in Cancer or Capricorn, it will be good. Let the author of light [the Sun] be praised. If it falls in **Pisces**, it is good for **trees**. Let the Moon not be except in **fixed signs** <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius; signs associated with stability and endurance</note> and [especially] in **Cancer** or **Aquarius**.

### On the Purchase of Dogs

### The Purchase of Animals

It is necessary that the Ascendant and the Moon be in a sign of an animal <note>Zodiac signs representing animals, such as Aries (the Ram), Taurus (the Bull), or Leo (the Lion).</note>, or as it has always been, let the Lord of that sign be fortunate, and let the Lord of that same sign be received through another. And if the Lord of that sign was not a "Fortune" <term>Fortune (fortuna): a benefic planet like Jupiter or Venus that brings good luck</term>, let it not be hindered, provided it is in an aspect of friendship and receives the Moon. And if that animal was male, let the places be situated in masculine signs; if however it is female, let it be in the contrary. If the time was more suitable to hear of its heritage, let the Moon be in the sign signifying that limb/member, with a Fortune and an aspect that is according to the nature of that animal or similar to it. And if it was not for the sake of health, the aspect should be similar or perfect, and in no way should it be divided from the Ascendant and its Lord.

### Chapter 8: On the 8th House

<margin>Lord of the Midheaven</margin>
Since between any two people there may be a dispute <note>original: "pugnas," literally fights or battles</note>, the matter will be handled by the "Master" <term>The "Master" or "Lord" is the planet that rules a specific zodiac sign</term> of the Ascendant, representing the one who seeks the answer, while the Midheaven <note>original: "mediu celi," the highest point in the sky at the time of the inquiry</note> represents the one who arbitrates between them. If it should be a war, the victory and the outcome will be for the people, and the Moon will be following or separating. Indeed, that planet from which the Moon separates is the Lord of the matter. Whether it regards that which is sought is doubtful; or perhaps the follower is then the one who favors the Sun. It is uncertain whether the Midheaven acts through dignity <note>Essential dignity: a planet's strength based on its position</note> or through an aspect; and if the Ascendant, the Part, or the Moon is stronger, it will favor the partnership.

<margin>Lord of the Moon</margin>
If, however, the sign is one of two bodies <term>Mutable signs (Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces), which were thought to represent duality or change</term> and the end is doubtful, let the house of the Moon be in the first of the two bodies, or in a place and circles where the agreements are settled.

### On Buying and Selling

<margin>Lord of the thing</margin>
It must be known that the Lord of the Ascendant belongs to the seller and his house <note>original: "domus"</note>, while the Midheaven, its house, and its Part belong to the thing being sold. The planet from which the Moon separates will be that of the seller, and the Moon itself represents the thing being sold. The planet toward which the Moon moves belongs to the buyer. It is not bad if the Moon is in the Ascendant's mansions for the sake of the sale, though it may hold it in hatred. <note>original: "odio habebat," an astrological term for a planet in a sign where it lacks dignity or is "detrimented."</note>

### On the Judgments of Betrothals

<margin>Ascendant</margin>
Let the Ascendant be a sign of signs <note>possibly referring to choosing a particularly strong sign</note> and better things, such as Taurus or Leo. The Ascendant and its Lord represent the man, and the [seventh] Lord represents the woman. They look to the man through the Sun and the planet from which the Moon separates; for the woman, they look to Venus and the planet to which the Moon is joined. The Midheaven will indicate what the future shall be between them in the end and in whatever regions.

<column-break/>

They shall be taught: if the "followers" <note>The planets moving toward an aspect</note> of the man and woman are in masculine signs, it will be better for the man, and the opposite must be said for the woman. If the follower of the man is in masculine planets, but that of the woman is in feminine ones, it signifies a balance for both. If then he receives the follower, the Moon separates from the dead <note>original: "morticut," likely a scribal error for "mortuis" or a similar technical term</note> planets and joins a higher planet, and the Moon itself stands against both. One indeed [is] for the children, and she held hatred from this proposal. The same work applies to elections in buying, seizing, and for the causes of actions concerning mentioned things; something is captured, but not burned.

### Chapter 9: On the Perfection of Houses

This entry concerns how to proceed in matters of water, for which the house is liberated by Jupiter and Venus. Let its Lord also be in aspect with the "Angles" <term>The four cardinal points of a chart: Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli</term>. If it is in these, your health and that of the house and its Lord will be good. If by chance it happens that the degree of the 8th house is the end <note>original: "finis," likely the "term" or "bound"</note> of Jupiter or Venus, it will be good. The Moon must also be watched so that the ruler of the 8th house appears in a praiseworthy aspect, and in these matters, it shall radiate from there.

### Chapter 10: On Temporal Dignity

Let the Moon and the Ascendant be in northern signs <note>original: "signis trioni," likely referring to the northern triplicity</note> of the houses which are called "of the sky." You will come to that in a better way. Let it be by way of age, and let its Lord be in agreement in leading toward the Ascendant. Let the Moon be with Mars, or joined to it in a friendly aspect. Let the position of Mercury be good and fortunate, and let their strengths be praised so that it is more appropriate for the ruler of the Ascendant. Let the Moon not be hindered in its course, nor should it be falling from its apogee. This is also fitting if the Lord is in the southern part. All these things prepare the work of writing and its memory, and the work to be undertaken will have a good increase in the first mention in this heavenly hour.

# Second, on the Education of Singers <note>original: "secunm de erudicione cannletarn," likely *secundum de erudicione cantilenarum*</note>

The Ascendant <term>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the time of the election</term> should be placed in the fourth [house], and the Sun should be in the sign of its dignity <term>Essential Dignity: the inherent strength of a planet based on its position in the zodiac</term>. A similar method should be observed regarding the Moon in the sign of its dignity, such as when it is found in Pisces, separated from Mercury and Libra, according to the days of Venus. If the Moon aspects <term>Aspect: the geometric angle between planets that determines their influence on one another</term> the house of the dignity of Venus, this work will be good under the aspect of the dignity of Venus and Mercury. Venus and Mercury should not be hindered by the Moon; if the Moon is not in a place where it is good and fortunate and strong, then it will be necessary to wait until these things are more perfect. There are also other fortunate placements. If the first [planet] is fortunate and strong, it will be good.

Some have noted that the "touch" of the Moon is important; for example, if the Moon is in Cancer during the training of the voice, or under Jupiter when it is in Pisces. For the trumpet, let it be in Leo; for singing voices, let it be in the "fixed" signs. Signs that possess a "voice" <note>Gemini, Virgo, Libra, and Aquarius were traditionally called "vocal signs" because they are represented by human figures</note> are good for songs and chants and for making music <note>original: "mus dulandū," likely *modulandum*</note>, especially Gemini and Virgo. We are suited to this matter if the Lord [of the sign] is favorable, and if the Moon is in an advantageous position for the work you are preparing, it will be a good beginning for that matter.

### Chapter 11: On Swimming

It is necessary that the Moon and the Lord <note>original: "hyas," likely a shorthand for the *Hylech* or the governing planet</note> be in water signs. Let the Lord of the aspect be in the Midheaven <note>The highest point in the sky at the time of the election</note>, and let Venus be strong and fortunate toward it. The Moon should also aspect Scorpio—which is a sign of its dignity—though Cancer is better.

### On the Training for Fighting

It is necessary that the Moon and the aspect be in the triplicity <term>A group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water)</term> of Mars. Mars should be in a good position, and the Moon should not fall into a weak place, especially in military training. And if the Moon

<column-break/>

is in its exaltation <term>The sign where a planet's influence is most powerful</term>, it will be good. A similar rule applies to the aspect; if it cannot be in the Midheaven, then let it approach it. Some have said that for the training of wrestling, the Moon should be in Scorpio, or in the signs for the training of various arts.

One should choose a time that regards the work and its Lord under the Moon, and you should place the Part [of Fortune] and the Lord of the work according to the water of their dignities, making them fortunate and strong. For example, assign Mars to blacksmiths and servants, and the Sun to those who travel or work with gold. Place Mercury for those things that require subtlety of mind, such as the formation of images or the use of an astrolabe <note>original: "astrolapp," an ancient instrument used to calculate the positions of celestial bodies</note>. This will be good if the Moon is placed in its own dignity and joined through a clear reception <term>Reception: when one planet is in the sign ruled by another, creating a cooperative relationship</term> with Venus. If it is in the house of a planet that pertains to that work, it will be especially good. Let the Ascendant come to the appropriate place for the matter, and also the location of the figure, such as the earthly signs for those who work the earth, and aquatic signs for those who work with water.

### Chapter 12: On Exercising the Body

When you wish to begin exercising, the Moon should aspect its own lords. Place the Ascendant in the fourth [house], or in an aspect that appears favorable. It is necessary that Jupiter be strong and free, and the Lord [of the sign] should be in aspect so that whatever is done will be good. You should also place the Moon in a free position, joined to the Sun from a trine <term>Trine: a harmonious 120-degree aspect between two planets</term>, and let Mars be in the fourth house, or restored to the eleventh, and joined to Jupiter.

<meta>This page continues the technical discussion of the celestial sphere, specifically focusing on the relationships between zodiac signs and their elemental, seasonal, and physiological influences.</meta>

### On the Sphere

<margin>Signs clearly distinguished</margin>
...ascending from the beginning of Aries until the end of Sagittarius, and they are opposite, ascending tortuously <note>the 'tortuous' or 'crooked' signs (Aries through Virgo) are those that rise more slowly in the northern hemisphere</note>, they return; then from the beginning of Capricorn until the end of Gemini, they also ascend tortuously and "obey" those that ascend directly. That is, the lord of the sign which was of equal length from the head of Aries to some part of the mid-heaven is "obedient." For example, Gemini obeys Cancer, Taurus obeys Aries, Virgo obeys Leo, Pisces obeys Libra, Aquarius obeys Scorpio, and Capricorn
<margin>Concordant signs</margin>
obeys Sagittarius. And since all the lengths from the head of Aries were called concordant, they would draw together: Aries and Pisces, Taurus and Aquarius, Gemini and Capricorn, and Cancer and Sagittarius. Libra therefore looks upon the two aforementioned [halves]: that which is from the beginning of Aries to the end of Cancer, which is half of the world according to the movement of the signs, which pertains to the solar year. This is the hot half, for the Sun is in these parts... <unclear>the highest</unclear> and others... from the beginning of Aquarius to the end of Cancer... properly on the part of the signs... for Mars and it is the middle in which the Moon has a son <note>This likely refers to astrological "exaltations" or planetary domiciles</note>... in this perverse half... the Sun's terms... and in that very half which is from the beginning of Aries to the end of <unclear>Cancer</unclear>, it is properly the hot half, because in you...

<column-break/>

it makes summer for us; and the other, which is from the beginning of Libra to the end of Pisces, is the cold half. This is opposite to the whole [universe]. By the circle <note>reading 'oculi' as a transcription error for 'circuli'</note> which is from the beginning of Aries to the end of Gemini, it is hot and moist, properly belonging to <term>blood</term> <note>original: "sangui"; refers to the Sanguine humor, associated with Spring</note>. And the other, which is from the beginning of Cancer to the end of Virgo, is hot and dry, summer-like, youthful <note>original: "inuencibilis", likely "iuvenilis"</note>, and <term>choleric</term> <note>original: "colerica"; associated with yellow bile</note>. And the third, which is from the beginning of Libra to the end of Sagittarius, is said to be cold and dry, autumnal, and <term>melancholic</term> <note>original: "melancolica"; associated with black bile</note>. These are the signs of diminishing [light]. And that which is from the beginning of Capricorn to the end of Pisces is cold and moist, a time of decline for the elderly, which is wintery <note>original: "vernalis", though the context implies "hyemalis"</note> and produces our <term>phlegm</term> <note>original: "fleuma"; the Phlegmatic humor</note>.

***

**Image Description:**
A circular diagram illustrating the Four Seasons and the Four Humors as they relate to the Zodiac.
- **Spring (Top-Right):** Aries, Taurus, Gemini. Hot and moist. Humor: Blood (*sanguis*).
- **Summer (Bottom-Right):** Cancer, Leo, Virgo. Hot and dry. Humor: Red Bile/Choler (*colera rubea*).
- **Autumn (Bottom-Left):** Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius. Cold and dry. Humor: Melancholy (*melancolia*).
- **Winter (Top-Left):** Capricorn, Aquarius, Pisces. Cold and moist. Humor: Phlegm (*fleuma*).

<summary>This page details the astrological concept of "obedient signs" and maps the twelve signs of the zodiac to the four seasons, the four elemental qualities, and the four human humors.</summary>
<keywords>astrology, zodiac, humors, sanguine, choleric, melancholic, phlegmatic, seasons, obedient signs, medieval medicine</keywords>
